The package is explicitly targeted at segments of the electorate, including small-business owners and students, in an effort to gain support against the opposition candidate, Flávio Bolsonaro.

policydecision_details: Togo is introducing a new complaint-handling system for the $62.5 million SWEDD+ project to improve beneficiary participation and oversight. The system will operate through local committees at various administrative levels, allowing residents to report problems, request information, and raise concerns regarding project activities. Complainants are expected to receive an acknowledgment within two days, with a resolution target of 20 days. The initiative emphasizes the confidentiality and safety of participants, particularly in addressing gender-based violence.
contextoradditionalinfo: The SWEDD+ project, funded by the World Bank, aims to improve access to education, healthcare, and economic opportunities for women and girls in Togo. The introduction of this complaint-handling mechanism is intended to strengthen accountability and ensure that project activities effectively reach and support the intended beneficiaries in communities across the country.

policydecision_details: The government of Niger has implemented a restriction on the export of gasoline and diesel to prioritize domestic supply. Under the new order, domestically produced fuel must be reserved for the local market to address persistent shortages at service stations. Exports are now only permitted in cases of surplus and require special authorization from the Minister of Trade and Industry. Enforcement of these measures is assigned to the Ministry of Trade, customs officers, and the Defense and Security Forces.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced following weeks of severe fuel shortages at service stations across Niger. The country's only refinery in Zinder has struggled to meet the national daily consumption demand of 2.5 million liters of gasoline and up to 2 million liters of diesel. The situation was exacerbated by a decline in informal fuel imports from neighboring Nigeria, which previously accounted for half of national consumption, forcing more demand onto official service stations.

policydecision_details: Burkina Faso has launched a public bond offering worth CFA100 billion ($171.2 million) on the regional financial market. The subscription period for this bond issue is open from October 12 to October 30, 2026. The offering is structured into three fixed-rate tranches with maturities of five, seven, and 10 years, offering interest rates of 6.60%, 6.75%, and 7% respectively. The proceeds from this issuance are intended to finance the country's 2026 national budget.
contextoradditionalinfo: The government is increasingly relying on the regional West African Monetary Union (WAMU) debt market to meet its financing needs due to the lack of an international credit rating. This borrowing strategy is driven by tight budgetary conditions, including high security spending related to the fight against jihadist groups and significant infrastructure investment requirements. Despite these pressures, the IMF has assessed the country's public debt as sustainable with a moderate risk of distress.

policydecision_details: Benin has signed two cofinancing agreements with the Islamic Development Bank totaling $364.4 million to support infrastructure and agricultural development. The first component allocates €306.89 million for the upgrading of the Godomey-Ouidah-Hillacondji road to improve trade and transport efficiency. The second component provides €19.17 million to enhance the productivity and sustainability of legume-based farming systems across five agricultural zones. These projects aim to strengthen food security, improve soil fertility, and increase climate resilience for local farms.
contextoradditionalinfo: The agreements were signed during the annual meetings of the World Bank Group and the IMF to address infrastructure gaps and agricultural productivity challenges in Benin. The country has been actively increasing investments in road networks and rural tracks to facilitate trade along the Abidjan-Lagos corridor and improve access to markets. Additionally, the government is prioritizing sustainable farming practices to support the agricultural sector, which accounts for over 40% of national employment.

policydecision_details: Announced a €5.9 billion budget for the justice sector for 2027, representing an increase of over €400 million. The funding supports frontline services including An Garda Síochána, the Irish Prison Service, and the Irish Courts Service. Key allocations include €84.4 million for domestic, sexual and gender-based violence services and €14.5 million for civil legal aid reforms. The budget also prioritizes prison capacity expansion and youth justice initiatives.
contextoradditionalinfo: The budget announcement, published on 8 October 2026, aims to modernize the justice sector, improve public safety, and strengthen rehabilitation and victim support services. It reflects a strategic shift in government spending to address crime prevention and social service delivery. Additionally, the budget includes reforms to the immigration system to increase efficiency and reduce accommodation costs.
beneficiaries: victims of domestic, sexual and gender-based violence, youth, prisoners

policydecision_details: The Irish Government, in partnership with the EIB Group and the Strategic Banking Corporation of Ireland, has expanded the Growth and Sustainability Loan Scheme from €500 million to €1 billion. This initiative provides long-term, affordable finance to SMEs, including those in the agricultural, forestry, and fishing sectors. The scheme aims to support business expansion, innovation, and sustainable operating models, with a requirement that at least 30% of lending volume be directed toward environmental sustainability. The program is now extended until 30 June 2029 to ensure continued support for economic resilience and climate action.
contextoradditionalinfo: The expansion follows the successful deployment of the initial €500 million capacity launched in September 2023, which supported approximately 2,000 businesses. The government aims to further strengthen the enabling conditions for sustainable livelihoods and climate resilience by providing lower-cost credit compared to standard commercial lending. This measure is part of a broader strategy to foster job creation and sustainable growth across all Irish regions.
decision_making_institution: European Investment Bank (EIB) Group, Irish Government, and Strategic Banking Corporation of Ireland (SBCI)
beneficiaries: small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), farmers, foresters, fishers

policydecision_details: The Ukrainian parliament has approved the first reading of a bill designed to accelerate the privatization of state-owned assets. The legislation introduces a strict 20-day deadline for state bodies to transfer assets to the State Property Fund, preventing indefinite delays. It also proposes the creation of a state-owned consulting firm to manage the preparation of assets for auction. This measure aims to improve the efficiency of the privatization process and generate revenue for the state budget. The bill is expected to be adopted by early December.
contextoradditionalinfo: Ukraine is facing a severe budget shortfall and is under pressure from international partners, including the IMF and World Bank, to reform its state-owned enterprise sector. The current privatization process is hindered by bureaucratic bottlenecks, where ministries and local authorities delay the transfer of assets to the State Property Fund. The government intends to reduce its portfolio of approximately 3,000 assets to 100 key enterprises to attract investment and improve economic efficiency.

policydecision_details: Announced the release of 2.5 million hectares of state-owned land to Black farmers. The land will be transferred with title deeds under the Proactive Land Acquisition Strategy. This initiative aims to integrate more farmers into commercial production and address historical racial disparities in land ownership. The government also emphasizes the need for accompanying support, including affordable financing, mentorship, and training to ensure sustainable farming operations.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy addresses the legacy of apartheid, which left a sector marked by stark racial disparities where white South Africans hold approximately 75% of private land compared to 4% held by Black citizens. The initiative is part of a broader effort to transform the agricultural sector and improve the participation of Black farmers in commercial agriculture, who currently represent only about 10% of the sector.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: The Mozambican government has secured 47 million dollars to support climate change mitigation and adaptation efforts. As part of this initiative, the government has devised a plan to address water-related issues caused by the El Niño weather phenomenon. The strategy focuses on the agricultural sector, specifically through the distribution of inputs and the implementation of irrigation systems. These measures are designed to support farmers in the short and medium term to ensure production stability.
contextoradditionalinfo: Mozambique is facing significant climate-related challenges, including the impacts of the El Niño weather phenomenon which threatens water availability and agricultural productivity. To address these risks, the government is collaborating with international partners like Belgium and the UK to mobilize climate finance. This funding is intended to strengthen the country's resilience and support the National Development Strategy 2025-2034.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: The Government of Mozambique has announced the 2026–2035 Public Finance Management Strategy (EGFP) aimed at increasing tax revenue from 17% to 26.2% of GDP by 2035. The reform focuses on broadening the tax base, integrating the informal economy, and taxing digital activities. It also introduces green taxation based on the 'polluter pays' principle to support climate adaptation and mitigation. These measures are designed to reduce dependence on external financing and create fiscal space for public investment and social policies.
contextoradditionalinfo: The strategy was developed in response to severe financial constraints caused by high civil service wages and debt servicing, which currently absorb 90% of state revenue. Public debt indicators have deteriorated significantly, with debt stock rising from 30% to 43% between 2020 and 2025. The government aims to improve fiscal sustainability to ensure the country can fund priority social and economic development programs.

policydecision_details: The Central Bank of Sri Lanka implemented macroprudential measures to contain systemic financial risks, including tightening loan-to-value (LTV) limits on vehicle and gold-backed lending. The overnight policy interest rate was increased in May 2026 to address inflationary pressures and credit growth. Additionally, the Central Bank issued directives for relief measures to be provided to individuals and businesses affected by Cyclone Ditwah. These actions aim to strengthen the resilience of the banking and finance company sectors while ensuring financial stability.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Financial Stability Review for 2026 identified a rapid expansion in private sector credit, particularly in household lending, which signaled a potential build-up of systemic vulnerabilities. The financial system faced challenges from global geopolitical tensions, inflationary pressures, and the impact of Cyclone Ditwah. These factors necessitated regulatory interventions to mitigate credit risk, manage liquidity, and ensure the operational resilience of the financial sector.

policydecision_details: The Health Sciences Authority (HSA) has announced three new initiatives to accelerate the approval of healthcare innovations, including AI-based therapies. These measures include a regulatory innovation corridor with the UK's MHRA, a common entry point for clinical research, and a priority track for concurrent regulatory and health technology assessments. These changes are expected to halve approval times for certain Phase 3 clinical trials and significantly shorten health technology assessment timelines. The initiatives aim to position Singapore as a trusted regulatory hub while maintaining high safety and effectiveness standards.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to help promising healthcare innovations reach patients sooner and to ensure Singapore's regulatory framework keeps pace with evolving healthcare delivery models and medical technology. By consolidating regulatory functions under the HSA and strengthening international partnerships, the government aims to create a more coherent, future-ready healthcare ecosystem. This approach is designed to provide clarity for the industry while protecting patients and addressing changing population needs.

policydecision_details: Prime Minister has instructed ministries and institutions to prioritize disaster risk management as a core task to enhance national resilience. The directive mandates the implementation of the National Action Plan on Disaster Risk Reduction 2024-2028 and the National Roadmap on Early Warning systems, in response of El Niño-linked drought affecting rice fields and widespread flooding. It emphasizes strengthening inter-ministerial coordination and capacity building to better manage climate-related hazards. Furthermore, the government aims to improve public awareness and ensure timely dissemination of early warning signs to protect vulnerable communities and infrastructure.
contextoradditionalinfo: Cambodia is facing increasingly frequent and intense climate-related disasters, including droughts and floods, which threaten economic growth and food security. Recent events, such as the El Niño-linked drought affecting 290,000 hectares of rice fields and widespread flooding in 2026, have highlighted gaps in community-level preparedness and water infrastructure. The government recognizes that climate change could significantly impact GDP by 2050, necessitating a more robust, integrated approach to disaster risk reduction and community resilience.
beneficiaries: smallholder farmers, vulnerable families, rural communities

policy_description: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations
policydecision_details: The Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy has announced a partnership with Norway to combat illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing in Nigerian waters. Nigeria will join the 'Blue Justice' initiative, which provides access to satellite-based Automatic Identification System (AIS) vessel-tracking data. This technology will enable authorities to monitor maritime activities, identify 'dark vessels' that evade tracking, and investigate suspicious movements. The initiative aims to protect marine resources, safeguard the livelihoods of local fishers, and ensure the sustainable management of aquatic resources.
contextoradditionalinfo: The government expressed concern that foreign operators are illegally harvesting fish from Nigerian waters, which are then sold back to Nigerians at high prices. This practice undermines local livelihoods, deprives the country of economic benefits, and threatens the sustainability of fish stocks. The partnership is part of a broader effort to boost local fish production, reduce import dependence, and conserve foreign exchange.
decision_making_institution: Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy
policycategory: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations

policydecision_details: The World Bank Group is mobilizing $6 billion in private financing for Nigeria to support agriculture, MSMEs, and job creation. Key initiatives include the AGROW project, which targets one million smallholder farmers by improving seed and fertilizer systems and market access. The FINCLUDE program aims to provide financial support to over 250,000 MSMEs to boost productivity and employment. These efforts are part of a broader strategy to leverage private capital through reforms, risk-sharing tools, and public-private partnerships. The initiative is expected to support 850,000 direct and indirect jobs by 2030.
contextoradditionalinfo: Since mid-2023, Nigeria has implemented significant economic reforms, including foreign-exchange management, public finance strengthening, and fuel subsidy reforms. These measures aim to create a more predictable investment environment. The World Bank Group is building on these reforms to translate improved conditions into concrete opportunities for private capital, addressing gaps in infrastructure, agricultural value chains, and financial access.

policydecision_details: The Federal Government of Nigeria is scaling up its school feeding initiative in Niger State to prioritize the use of locally sourced, nutritious foods. The program aims to improve child nutrition, cognitive development, and school attendance while simultaneously supporting local farmers and food producers. By integrating local agricultural products into school meals, the government seeks to strengthen local food systems and provide economic opportunities for women and small-scale participants in the value chain. Training sessions for women on preparing nutritious meals are a key component of this initiative to ensure long-term health benefits for children.
contextoradditionalinfo: The initiative is part of a broader federal strategy to address hunger and malnutrition among children from vulnerable and economically disadvantaged households. It recognizes that adequate nutrition is essential for physical and cognitive growth, and that investing in child nutrition is a strategic investment in Nigeria's human capital and future productivity. The program also aims to foster collaboration between the federal government, state governments, and local stakeholders to promote sustainable development and poverty reduction.
decision_making_institution: Federal Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction
additionalcommodities: Cereals and cereal products|Meat and other animal derived products|Roots and tubers and derived products

policydecision_details: The Alentejo 2030 programme has launched a €3.525 million funding initiative to support SMEs in hiring highly qualified professionals. The programme offers two distinct calls for proposals, with one specifically targeting businesses in low-density areas and the other for those in non-low-density areas. This initiative is co-financed by the European Social Fund Plus (ESF+) at a rate of 50 percent. The funding aims to strengthen innovation capacity, facilitate technology transfer, and promote sustainable, quality employment within the region. Applications for these grants are open until March 31, 2027.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Alentejo region aims to boost its business competitiveness and accelerate organisational and technological modernisation. By incentivizing the hiring of graduates, researchers, and other highly qualified human resources, the programme seeks to bridge the gap between local companies and the regional scientific and technological system. This is part of a broader strategy to foster innovation and economic development in the Alentejo region.
decision_making_institution: Alentejo Regional Coordination and Development Commission (CCDR-AL)
beneficiaries: micro enterprises, small enterprises, medium-sized enterprises

policydecision_details: Expanded the Digital Work Card system to cover an additional 500,000 workers, bringing the total number of covered employees to approximately 2.5 million. This initiative aims to ensure that workers are accurately compensated for their actual working hours. By digitizing work records, the system enhances transparency and helps combat undeclared or underreported employment. The expansion is part of a phased rollout that includes full implementation for specific sectors starting in November 2026.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Digital Work Card was introduced to address issues of undeclared labor and ensure fair compensation. Previous pilot phases and implementations in sectors like wholesale trade, tourism, and hospitality have demonstrated significant increases in declared overtime hours, suggesting the system effectively captures previously unrecorded labor activity.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Labour and Social Security

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: Introduced a draft law to ban social media access for minors under the age of 15, effective January 1, 2027. This measure aims to protect children from digital risks such as excessive use, cyberbullying, and exposure to inappropriate content. The regulation will utilize age verification technologies that prioritize privacy, such as zero-knowledge proof, to ensure compliance without requiring identity documents. The government plans to systematically evaluate the implementation of this policy with support from scientific experts, parents, and teachers.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was developed in response to growing concerns from parents, teachers, and experts regarding the impact of social media on the wellbeing of minors. It serves as a proactive national measure ahead of a broader, ongoing European legislative initiative known as the EU KIDS Act. The government seeks to balance the protection of children with their rights to information and communication.
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation has approved EGP 80.885 million in new funding for the National Veal Project. This initiative provides financial support to small-scale breeders and young graduates to raise and fatten 1,148 head of cattle. The funding is part of the broader presidential Decent Life initiative aimed at rural development. The project seeks to increase domestic supplies of red meat and dairy products to ensure market stability and food security.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is designed to address domestic food supply gaps and protect citizens from global market fluctuations. By supporting small-scale livestock production, the government aims to improve rural household incomes, create job opportunities, and ensure that essential food commodities remain available at fair prices.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

policydecision_details: The Kenyan government has introduced the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026, which prohibit the washing or embalming of bodies of individuals who die from Ebola. The regulations mandate that victims must be buried in the country where they die, effectively banning the repatriation of bodies of Kenyans who die abroad from the virus. Furthermore, the rules prohibit the undressing or redressing of bodies for funeral purposes and require that bodies be transported in sealed bags under strict infection control measures. These measures are designed to prevent the importation and spread of the Ebola virus within Kenya.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced following Kenya's first imported case of the Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease, involving a citizen who traveled from the Democratic Republic of Congo through Uganda to Nairobi. The government aims to mitigate the risk of further virus importation and manage public health safety during the potential outbreak. The regulations align with WHO guidance on infection prevention and control for Ebola-related deaths.

policydecision_details: Brazil's National Technical Biosafety Commission (CTNBio) has officially approved a new stacked-trait genetically modified soybean event developed by the Brazilian unit of Beijing Dabeinong (DBN) Technology Group. The approved event, DBN9004 x DBN8002 x DBN8205, integrates two herbicide-tolerance genes and three insect-resistance genes into a single seed. This regulatory milestone allows for the future commercialization of the seed following necessary multiplication and registration steps. The decision marks a significant expansion of Chinese biotechnology firms into the Brazilian agricultural market.
contextoradditionalinfo: The approval reflects a broader trend of Chinese agricultural biotechnology companies increasing their presence in Brazil, the world's largest soybean producer. By stacking multiple traits, the new seed aims to provide growers with more effective weed control and resistance management against major lepidopteran pests like the fall armyworm, which have shown increasing resistance to older single-gene traits. This move diversifies the trait-licensing market, which has historically been dominated by a few Western multinational corporations.

policydecision_details: Côte d’Ivoire has inaugurated a new processing plant in Kongodékro to strengthen its shea and oilseed processing industry. The facility, operated by BETA VEG OIL, has an annual processing capacity of 70,000 tonnes of raw materials, including shea kernels and soybeans. This investment aims to retain more agricultural value within the country by transforming raw materials into higher-value products like shea butter and soybean oil. The government is also implementing measures to regulate marketing channels and secure supplies for local industries to improve capacity utilization.
contextoradditionalinfo: The country has approximately 20 processing units with an installed capacity of 130,000 tonnes of shea kernels, but a significant portion remains underutilized. To address this, the government has prohibited the export of raw shea nuts and kernels across land borders since January 2025 and is prioritizing local processing units for raw material purchases. These efforts are part of a broader strategy to increase domestic value addition and support the local agricultural supply chain.
beneficiaries: oilseed processors, shea producers, soybean producers

policydecision_details: The National Bank of Serbia has decided to maintain its benchmark interest rate at 5.75%. This decision reflects a cautious monetary stance in response to rising energy costs and inflationary pressures. The central bank aims to balance the need for price stability with the requirement to support economic growth and investment. The policy remains in effect as the bank monitors the potential pass-through of industrial producer price increases to the broader economy.
contextoradditionalinfo: Annual inflation in Serbia is projected to approach 4% by September 2026, driven by higher oil, gas, and electricity costs. These rising industrial costs threaten to erode corporate margins and complicate financing for manufacturers, particularly in energy-intensive sectors. While the economy shows signs of growth, the central bank is concerned that persistent energy inflation could limit its ability to ease monetary policy, thereby impacting corporate borrowing and investment.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The Nigerian government is partnering with international manufacturers to establish domestic solar panel production capacity. This initiative aims to strengthen quality control and reduce reliance on imported solar components, which are currently subject to potential future restrictions. The government is also implementing the 'Renewed Hope Solarisation Project' to provide renewable energy to public institutions. Additionally, the policy includes training programs for artisans to build a skilled workforce for solar manufacturing and installation.
contextoradditionalinfo: Nigeria faces a significant electricity deficit and high dependence on expensive fossil fuel generators. The government seeks to transition to renewable energy while ensuring that local industrial capacity is sufficient to prevent price hikes that would occur if solar imports were restricted prematurely. The strategy focuses on a 'manufacturing-first' approach to ensure long-term energy security and affordability.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Signed a $362 million Public-Private Partnership agreement to establish a fully integrated titanium processing plant. The state has allocated 100.079 hectares of land for the project and will provide regulatory support and infrastructure. This joint venture aims to process ilmenite ore into titanium dioxide and titanium sponge. The project is expected to create over 800 direct jobs and generate significant annual economic value for the state and the nation.
contextoradditionalinfo: The initiative is part of Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa’s industrialization agenda, which seeks to leverage state resources to create local jobs and ensure sustained revenue. By processing raw minerals locally instead of exporting them, the project aims to integrate Nigeria into global aerospace and defense supply chains.
commodity1: Other products, not included in the other categories

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: Developed a new directive to regulate the use of artificial intelligence (AI) within the financial sector. This policy aims to foster innovation in areas such as credit assessment, fraud detection, and risk management while ensuring appropriate governance. The directive will address emerging risks associated with AI, including data quality, cybersecurity, and consumer protection. It represents a broader effort by the central bank to strengthen regulatory frameworks in response to the digitalization of financial services.
contextoradditionalinfo: As digitalization transforms financial services in Ghana, the Bank of Ghana has identified the need to manage the risks introduced by new technologies. While AI offers potential benefits for operational efficiency and financial inclusion, it also creates new channels for risks like digital fraud and third-party dependencies. The Governor emphasized that regulatory frameworks must evolve to keep pace with technological change and interconnected financial risks.
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Advanced strategic energy infrastructure projects to connect Eastern Mediterranean natural gas fields and renewable electricity grids to European markets. The government is formalizing commercial and regulatory frameworks to process gas from Cypriot fields, such as Cronos and Aphrodite, through Egyptian liquefaction facilities. Additionally, the GREGY subsea cable project aims to export renewable electricity from Egypt to Greece. These initiatives are designed to position Egypt as a central regional energy trading hub while supporting supply diversification for Europe.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is driven by the need to maximize the utilization of Eastern Mediterranean gas resources and enhance regional energy connectivity. By integrating infrastructure with European networks, Egypt seeks to leverage its existing LNG export facilities at Damietta and Idku. This cooperation, discussed at the Eastern Mediterranean Gas Forum, aims to secure energy supplies for Europe while generating economic benefits for Egypt, Cyprus, and Greece.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: The Angolan Ministry of Public Works has launched the construction of a 255-km road to improve connectivity between municipalities. This infrastructure project is designed to facilitate trade and economic development in regions with high agricultural and tourism potential. The road will serve as a critical link for transporting local crops such as cassava, rice, cotton, corn, and peanuts to markets. The project is part of a broader national strategy to expand the road network and integrate economic centers into regional trade corridors. Construction is expected to span 24 months, with a total investment exceeding 211 billion kwanzas.
contextoradditionalinfo: Angola is currently implementing a large-scale infrastructure development program to diversify its economy away from oil dependency. By improving transport networks, including roads, ports, and railways, the government aims to position the country as a regional transit hub for trade and mineral exports. This specific road project addresses the need to better connect rural agricultural production areas to economic centers, thereby fostering regional integration and economic growth.

policydecision_details: The government of Benin has secured an $18.4 million grant from Japan to finance the second phase of the Vêdoko interchange project in Cotonou. This funding will cover the construction of an east-west overpass and related road improvements to complement the ongoing first phase. The project aims to reduce traffic congestion and improve the movement of people and goods across the city. It is a critical component of efforts to enhance urban mobility and facilitate trade along the Abidjan-Lagos corridor.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Vêdoko intersection is a major bottleneck in Cotonou, with traffic projected to triple by 2035. The infrastructure project is essential for managing urban growth and supporting the Abidjan-Lagos trade route, which is vital for regional economic activity and the movement of goods. The project also addresses the high volume of two-wheeled vehicles that dominate local traffic.

policydecision_details: The government of Tanzania is developing a unified National Investment Policy to ease business constraints and improve access to finance and land. The reform aims to formalize informal businesses, allowing them to access credit, markets, and social protection services. By creating a clear legal framework through a proposed Private Sector Act, the government intends to strengthen private sector participation in the economy. These measures are designed to support the country's ambition of building a trillion-dollar economy by 2050 under the Dira 2050 vision.
contextoradditionalinfo: Many businesses in Tanzania operate informally, which prevents them from accessing essential services like credit, technology, and insurance. The current business environment presents persistent challenges for domestic investors, and the government seeks to replace the 2022 policy with a more comprehensive framework to unlock private sector potential and mobilize capital for key sectors including agriculture and manufacturing.

policydecision_details: The Russian government has partially lifted its ban on diesel exports, allowing for the sale of 500,000 tons of diesel to foreign markets. This decision follows a deal between Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Trump. Russian oil companies are authorized to immediately begin contracting for the sale of diesel fuel to international buyers. The government maintains that this easing of restrictions will not negatively impact domestic fuel supply or consumer prices.
contextoradditionalinfo: Russia originally implemented a ban on diesel exports in July 2026 following Ukrainian strikes on oil facilities that severely disrupted the country's fuel supply. The country had previously been forced to import fuel from India and permit the production of lower-grade gasoline to manage the shortage. The current partial lifting of the ban is linked to a broader diplomatic deal between the Russian and U.S. administrations.

policydecision_details: The Mozambican government plans to strengthen the Agrarian Sector Coordination Committee (CCSA) to serve as a central platform for setting investment priorities and mobilizing financing. This initiative aims to improve coordination among public institutions, producers, the private sector, and development partners following the conclusion of the Sustenta programme. The government intends to shift from a top-down approach by encouraging provincial and district-level institutions to participate actively in identifying problems and defining solutions. Furthermore, the ministry plans to integrate agriculture, environment, and fisheries sectors into a unified strategic framework for the 2027 budget cycle.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy follows the closure of the Sustenta programme, which previously defined the agricultural development strategy. The government is seeking a new approach to agricultural development that addresses resource constraints and improves the effectiveness of public interventions by fostering better collaboration and local participation.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Agriculture, Environment and Fisheries

policy_description: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget
policydecision_details: The Ministry of Finance has released a 'citizen budget' for the fiscal year 2083/84 to enhance transparency and public understanding of government spending. This publication serves as a simplified version of the existing budget and programs rather than a new legislative act. It outlines the annual budget cycle, key objectives, and fiscal policy features, including tax reforms and expenditure allocations. The document provides detailed information on benefits for specific groups and clarifies fiscal federalism frameworks. It aims to foster accountability by making the state's allocation process accessible to the general public.
contextoradditionalinfo: The initiative was introduced to improve transparency and accountability in the state's spending and allocation process. By simplifying complex fiscal data into a 'citizen budget,' the government aims to empower citizens to better understand tax usage and budget priorities. This effort aligns with the goal of promoting good governance and providing clarity on policy and legal reforms.
policycategory: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The Nigerian government is prioritizing the expansion of domestic solar panel manufacturing capacity through international partnerships and investment attraction before implementing any restrictions on solar panel imports. The initiative aims to foster local industrialization and ensure that solar energy remains affordable for households and businesses. The government is also establishing quality standards to prevent substandard components from entering the market. Additionally, a skills development program has been launched to train local artisans in solar manufacturing and installation.
contextoradditionalinfo: Nigeria faces significant electricity supply challenges, with the national grid providing only 4,000 to 5,000 megawatts for over 200 million people. Many consumers rely on expensive and polluting petrol or diesel generators to bridge the energy gap. Stakeholders warned that an immediate ban on solar imports would increase costs and hinder access to renewable energy, leading the government to adopt a phased approach that prioritizes local production capacity first.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: Introduced a bill to establish a minimum age of 15 for accessing social media platforms. This legislation aims to protect the health, safety, and social development of minors by restricting their access to online networking services. Oversight of the measure is assigned to the National Council for Radio and Television (ESR) and the Hellenic Data Protection Authority (DPA). The policy will be enforced using existing digital age-verification tools such as the Gov.gr Wallet and Kids Wallet applications.
contextoradditionalinfo: The government identified that early exposure to social media platforms, which utilize algorithms designed to maximize time spent online through personalized recommendations, increases the risk of problematic or addictive usage patterns among children. This preventive measure is intended to mitigate these risks and ensure a safer digital environment for minors.
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection

policydecision_details: Ethiopia has inaugurated a new precious metals refinery at the Bole Lemi Special Economic Zone to process gold domestically. The facility is a partnership between the state-owned Ethiopian Investment Holdings and Sam Precious Metals. It is designed to test, refine, and cast gold into bullion ready for export. This initiative aims to retain more value from the gold sector, which is a critical source of foreign-exchange earnings for the country.
contextoradditionalinfo: Gold is a major source of Ethiopia's foreign-exchange earnings, accounting for approximately half of the country's total export revenue in the 2025/26 fiscal year. Previously, raw gold was transported to Dubai for refining. The government established this facility to reduce reliance on overseas refineries and potentially serve as a regional hub for precious metals processing in Africa.

policydecision_details: Niger has reached a staff-level agreement with the IMF for a new $203 million financing programme under the Extended Credit Facility. The 38-month programme aims to strengthen macroeconomic stability, support financial sector reforms, and bolster the government's 2025–2029 development strategy. An initial disbursement of $36 million is expected upon approval by the IMF Executive Board. The funding will support fiscal capacity and government measures to assist households facing higher food and fuel prices.
contextoradditionalinfo: The agreement follows the IMF’s 2026 Article IV consultation and the final review of the country’s previous economic programme. While Niger's economy is projected to grow by 7% in 2026, the outlook is challenged by security threats, climate-related shocks, and international market volatility. The financing is intended to preserve economic progress and provide a buffer for households impacted by inflationary pressures on essential goods.

policy_description: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget
policydecision_details: The government of Burkina Faso has approved the draft state budget for 2027, totaling 4.8 trillion CFA francs in expenditure. The budget allocates funding to support agriculture, industry, the Armed Forces, and the social sector as part of the 2026–2030 economic recovery plan. Notably, the draft includes tax exemptions on egg sales and for travel agencies to stimulate economic activity. Additionally, the budget supports the construction of new healthcare facilities and the creation of a regional sports league.
contextoradditionalinfo: The budget is designed to implement the 2026–2030 national economic recovery plan, which aims to ensure security, improve governance, develop human capital, and strengthen the country's independence. The plan has a total projected budget of 36.19 trillion CFA francs.
beneficiaries: agricultural sector, industrial sector, travel agencies
policycategory: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget

policydecision_details: The government of Burkina Faso has proposed new legislation to tighten state control over strategic companies by prohibiting their privatization. The bill grants the government the authority to acquire equity stakes in both private and public entities classified as strategic. It introduces 'monopoly status' as a key criterion for identifying these strategic companies. This legislation is intended to replace the existing 1993 law to better align with current economic governance priorities. The proposal is currently awaiting review by the Transitional Legislative Assembly.
contextoradditionalinfo: This policy is part of a broader government strategy to increase public control over essential economic assets. Recent actions include the nationalization of the cotton company SOFITEX and increased state participation in the mining sector through SOPAMIB. The government aims to ensure that activities deemed essential to the national economy remain under public oversight.

policydecision_details: Announced a one-time intervention fund of Shs125 billion to empower health workers. This fund is designed to allow doctors to borrow capital for further professional specialization and to establish their own private businesses. Additionally, the President expressed support for tax exemptions for health workers and the creation of duty-free shops for essential health service items. The initiative aims to improve the welfare and career progression of medical professionals in Uganda.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy follows years of disagreements between medical interns and the government regarding allowances, deployment, and working conditions. Previous attempts to manage intern remuneration were hampered by financial constraints, leading to strikes and service disruptions. The President's decision seeks to balance the government's fiscal capacity with the need to support frontline health workers and improve the overall health sector.

policydecision_details: The Bank of Mozambique has extended the mandatory conversion of 50% of foreign currency export revenues into meticais for an additional six months. This measure requires exporters to convert half of their foreign currency earnings from goods, services, and overseas investments through the domestic banking system. The extension, formalized in Notice No. 7/GBM/2026, aims to maintain foreign exchange liquidity in the domestic market. The policy continues a transitional mechanism originally implemented in April 2025 to address ongoing challenges in accessing hard currency.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was extended due to persistent difficulties reported by businesses in accessing foreign currency, which has negatively impacted economic performance and revenue collection. While the central bank governor has disputed claims of a generalized shortage, the government acknowledged that scarcity of foreign currency hindered the payment of services and overall economic activity in the first half of 2026. The measure is intended to facilitate the financing of imports and international transactions amidst these socioeconomic constraints.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: Belgium and the European Union have mobilized $47 million to support Mozambique in strengthening climate resilience and expanding access to sustainable energy. The initiative involves the Belgian Development Agency, the National Energy Fund (FUNAE), and the National Climate Finance Directorate. Additionally, the government is implementing a short- and medium-term plan to mitigate the effects of the El Niño phenomenon, which includes the distribution of agricultural inputs and the reinforcement of irrigation systems. This intervention aims to support agricultural production in 52 districts identified as vulnerable to water scarcity.
contextoradditionalinfo: Mozambique is facing significant climate-related challenges, with 52 districts identified as being at risk from the El Niño phenomenon, which threatens water resources and agricultural production. The government is actively seeking climate finance to implement adaptation and mitigation measures, including the conversion of debt into environmental investments. The mobilization of these funds is part of a broader strategy to enhance national climate resilience and support the National Development Strategy 2025–2034.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policy_description: Subsidies on fuel, power and water
policydecision_details: The government of Cabo Verde is reviewing 2019 legislation to create more effective instruments for fuel price stabilization. This initiative aims to protect families, transport, fisheries, and businesses from volatile fuel price fluctuations. The government has allocated €10.8 million in the 2027 budget proposal to respond to ongoing price pressures. This review follows a recent 12% increase in petrol and diesel prices. The administration is prioritizing these measures to mitigate the impact of global inflation on the cost of living.
contextoradditionalinfo: The announcement was made by Prime Minister Francisco Carvalho during a presentation marking his administration's first 100 days. The government is facing significant economic challenges, including global inflation and rising fuel costs, which have negatively impacted the cost of living. The opposition has urged the government to reactivate previous price-limiting mechanisms. The government is also pursuing broader social and economic reforms, including investments in renewable energy, education, and water security.
policycategory: Subsidies on fuel, power and water

policydecision_details: Maritime Rules Part 91 – Navigation Safety Rules sets New Zealand’s national navigation safety standards for vessels operating in New Zealand waters, covering requirements such as personal flotation devices, vessel speed and wake limits, towing and water-skiing safety, anchoring, and other rules designed to promote safe boating. It also empowers harbourmasters and regional councils to enforce these standards, while requiring recreational craft to carry appropriately sized lifejackets for all persons on board and mandating their use in certain circumstances.
contextoradditionalinfo: Part 91 replaces the Water Recreation Regulations 1974.

policydecision_details: Algeria has secured a US$3 million export contract for plastic packaging products destined for the German market. This agreement marks a strategic shift for Algeria, moving beyond its traditional reliance on hydrocarbon and agricultural exports toward manufactured goods. The deal requires Algerian producers to meet stringent European standards, including material specifications and recycling compliance. This success is expected to encourage further industrial diversification and enhance the competitiveness of Algerian exports in international markets.
contextoradditionalinfo: The contract was announced during the Fruit Attraction 2026 trade fair in Madrid, where Algerian firms showcased agricultural and food products. The deal is part of a broader effort to facilitate agricultural exports to Europe by providing high-quality, compliant packaging solutions that meet international retail requirements. This initiative helps bridge the gap between Algerian production and European market access.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Foreign Trade and Export Promotion

policy_description: Subsidies on fuel, power and water
policydecision_details: Announced a series of interventions to mitigate the impact of high fuel prices without reversing the ongoing petrol subsidy reform. Key measures include NNPC Retail forgoing its profit margin to sell petrol at cost, particularly to commercial transport operators, and the negotiation of a price ceiling of N1,350 per litre. The government is also implementing forward sales of crude oil to domestic refineries to shield pump prices from global volatility. Additionally, the administration is expanding cash transfers, increasing subsidised credit for small businesses, and scaling up the deployment of Compressed Natural Gas (CNG). These interventions are designed to provide targeted support to vulnerable households and transport operators while maintaining the integrity of the deregulated fuel market.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced in response to the global petrol crisis and rising crude oil prices, which have caused significant economic hardship for Nigerian households. The government aims to balance the necessity of the petrol subsidy removal—which was implemented to prevent fiscal crisis and scarcity—with the need to protect the most vulnerable citizens from extreme price volatility and inflation.
policycategory: Subsidies on fuel, power and water
commodity1: Other products, not included in the other categories

policydecision_details: announced the Free State Catalytic Investment and Industrialisation Programme, a R120 billion initiative aimed at revitalizing the province's industrial sector. The program focuses on three key areas: renewable energy, electric vehicle manufacturing, and agricultural processing. By investing in infrastructure and municipal services, the government aims to attract private investment and create thousands of jobs. The initiative specifically seeks to link primary agricultural production to industrial processing and value addition to boost economic growth.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Free State province was a manufacturing hub until the early 2000s, but experienced a decline due to deteriorating municipal services and infrastructure, leading to business closures and relocations. The current initiative is part of the Free State Growth and Development Strategy, which aims to reverse this trend by leveraging the Maluti-a-Phofung Special Economic Zone. The government recognizes that reliable infrastructure and effective municipal services are essential to attract and retain investors in the region.
beneficiaries: small and medium-sized enterprises, local businesses, unemployed youth

policydecision_details: Declared 18 properties in the Eastern Cape as the Grasslands National Park. This declaration, published in Government Gazette No. 55531, covers over 10,000 hectares of land. The park is managed by South African National Parks (SANParks) and utilizes a biodiversity stewardship model that allows landowners to retain ownership while committing to conservation. This initiative aims to protect under-represented grassland ecosystems and a critical water source area while allowing for conservation-compatible agricultural activities.
contextoradditionalinfo: The declaration follows a multi-year statutory process initiated in 2025 to protect the Eastern Cape Drakensberg Strategic Water Source Area. The region is vital for water security, biodiversity, and the livelihoods of those working the agricultural land. By establishing the park through a stewardship model, the government seeks to demonstrate how conservation and productive land use can reinforce one another.
decision_making_institution: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Approved a fiscal exemption for Greece allowing up to €1 billion in energy-related investments to be excluded from EU net primary expenditure limits through 2028. The plan funds battery storage, heat pumps, solar water heaters, and energy efficiency upgrades for public buildings and schools. Additionally, it allocates resources for railway safety, industrial carbon capture, and energy transition support for specific regions. These investments are financed by national funds and aim to lower energy costs and strengthen energy independence.
contextoradditionalinfo: The measure was introduced to help Greece manage its energy transition and reduce exposure to international crises. By excluding these specific investments from EU fiscal growth limits, the government can pursue critical infrastructure and energy efficiency projects without violating primary budget balance and public debt constraints.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Finland will introduce a mandatory citizenship test starting 1 March 2027 for applicants aged 18 to 64. The test requires applicants to demonstrate knowledge of Finnish society, laws, history, and culture. It serves as the final stage of the government's program to tighten citizenship requirements. Applicants must pass the test before submitting their citizenship applications, though exemptions exist for certain educational qualifications or health conditions.
contextoradditionalinfo: The introduction of the citizenship test is part of a broader government initiative to tighten citizenship rules in Finland. This follows previous amendments that increased residency requirements and introduced stricter financial resource criteria for applicants.

country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
policydecision_details: The UK Office for SPS Trade Assurance has confirmed that no additional import restrictions are required following Albania's outbreak of sheep pox and goat pox (SPGP). Existing safeguard measures from June 2025, which suspended imports of untreated ovine and caprine wool and hair from Albania due to a previous PPR outbreak, remain in effect. These commodities continue to be ineligible for import into Great Britain. The status of SPGP in Albania will continue to dictate future import conditions for these products even if the previous PPR-related restrictions are lifted.
contextoradditionalinfo: Albania notified the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) on 23 September 2026 of an outbreak of sheep pox and goat pox (SPGP) in a mixed herd, resulting in the loss of its SPGP-free status. The UK government reviewed the situation and determined that existing import suspensions for untreated wool and hair from Albania, originally implemented for PPR, are sufficient to manage the risk.
decision_making_institution: UK Office for Sanitary and Phytosanitary (SPS) Trade Assurance

policydecision_details: The USDA has announced amendments to the federal marketing order for California raisins. These amendments, which were supported by producers in a referendum, authorize quality regulations and research and promotion programs. The Raisin Administrative Committee will continue to administer these industry-driven programs to help producers and handlers achieve marketing success. The final rule for this action was published in the Federal Register on October 9, 2026.
contextoradditionalinfo: Marketing orders are authorized by the Agricultural Marketing Agreement Act of 1937. They are industry-driven programs that allow producers and handlers to leverage their own funds to design and execute programs that they would not be able to do individually, ensuring fiscal accountability and program integrity.

policydecision_details: The French government agency Business France has opened a permanent office in Belgrade to facilitate commercial partnerships and investment between France and Serbia. This platform aims to support French companies entering the Serbian market and assist Serbian businesses in accessing the French market. The initiative focuses on sectors such as engineering, infrastructure, technology, and industrial cooperation. A formal cooperation agreement between Business France and the Serbian Chamber of Commerce is scheduled for November 30 to establish a long-term framework for these activities.
contextoradditionalinfo: The initiative responds to a growing bilateral trade relationship between France and Serbia, which is expected to reach €2.5 billion by the end of 2026. It seeks to integrate Serbian domestic engineering and technology companies into European project supply chains, particularly in infrastructure projects like the Belgrade Metro and municipal water management. The move represents a strategic effort to move beyond simple foreign investment toward deeper industrial and service-sector integration.
beneficiaries: Serbian companies, French companies, engineering firms, technology companies

policydecision_details: The Government of Japan has allocated approximately US$300,000 to fund three community-based projects in Paraguay through its Grant Assistance for Grassroots Human Security Projects (GGP) programme. The projects focus on improving drinking water access in the Cordillera Department, expanding educational facilities in the Central Department, and enhancing road infrastructure and stormwater drainage in Caraguatay. These initiatives aim to provide safe water to 4,000 people, support school infrastructure for 580 students and 60 teachers, and improve accessibility for 10,100 residents. The grant agreements were signed by the Japanese Ambassador to Paraguay and representatives of the beneficiary institutions.
contextoradditionalinfo: The GGP programme is part of Japan's official development assistance, which has been active in Paraguay since 1989 to address basic community needs. This initiative continues a long-standing partnership between the two countries, with 440 projects implemented to date focusing on education, health, and infrastructure to support local development.
beneficiaries: local communities, students, teachers, people with mobility challenges

policydecision_details: The Government of Liberia issued Executive Order 166, which imposes a ban on the export of all natural unprocessed rubber from Liberia. The order specifically prohibits the transshipment of unprocessed rubber originating from other countries, such as Guinea, through Liberian ports. This measure effectively halts the transit of rubber through the Freeport of Monrovia.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced as a moratorium on unprocessed rubber, ostensibly to regulate the domestic rubber sector. However, the inclusion of a ban on transshipment rubber has triggered a regional trade crisis with neighboring Guinea. The move has negatively impacted revenue collection at the border and disrupted the operations of local transport businesses.

policy_description: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget
policydecision_details: The government of Benin has approved a draft 2027 budget that represents a 14.7% increase over the revised 2026 budget. This fiscal plan prioritizes five key areas: modernizing agriculture, promoting industrial development, expanding tourism and culture, advancing technological innovation, and strengthening human capital. Public spending is specifically directed toward investments in education, health care, social protection, energy, and water to foster economic transformation. The draft has been submitted to the National Assembly for final review and approval.
contextoradditionalinfo: The budget proposal follows several years of strong economic growth in Benin, with the economy growing 8% in the first three quarters of 2025. The government aims to maintain this momentum while adhering to WAEMU convergence criteria, including a budget deficit ceiling of 3% of GDP and an inflation threshold of 3%. The policy is designed to consolidate ongoing economic transformation and address sociopolitical and security challenges through inclusive social and economic policies.
policycategory: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget

policy_description: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations
policydecision_details: The Stawi Bluu programme was launched to support tourism and aquaculture businesses in Tanzania through improved access to financing, markets, and skills. The initiative, funded by the EU and Germany, provides business development services, investment readiness, and training to enhance productivity and market connections. It specifically targets businesses in Dar es Salaam, Bagamoyo, Unguja, Pemba, and Mafia. The programme aims to promote the processing of aquatic products and the development of diversified tourism services to boost economic opportunities.
contextoradditionalinfo: The programme is part of the broader €110 million Team Europe Initiative on Blue Economy for Jobs and Climate Action in Tanzania, under the EU's Global Gateway strategy. It addresses the need for sustainable investment and climate resilience in marine and coastal sectors, following significant growth in tourism receipts and commercial aquaculture production in Tanzania.
decision_making_institution: European Union and Germany's Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development
policycategory: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations

policydecision_details: Announced a €7.597 billion budget package for 2027 aimed at enhancing childcare affordability, disability services, and child protection. Key measures include increasing universal childcare subsidies and reducing the maximum fees providers can charge under core funding. The budget also expands disability services, including new residential placements and increased staffing for disability network teams. Additionally, it provides increased support for child protection through Tusla and introduces new aftercare allowances for young people leaving state care.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of the Irish government's Budget 2027, designed to address the rising cost of living and support vulnerable populations. By integrating childcare affordability with disability and family support services, the government aims to create a more robust social safety net. The initiative reflects a strategic focus on improving access to essential services for families and children across the country.
beneficiaries: children, families, disabled people, vulnerable communities, early years educators

policydecision_details: The Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine has approved a new Procedure for the preparation and implementation of projects financed by loans from foreign governments and financial institutions. This resolution, developed by the Ministry of Finance, streamlines the process for attracting and utilizing external financing for public investment and priority development projects. It establishes clear criteria for selecting financial institutions and defines the entire lifecycle of loan documentation, from negotiation to disbursement and oversight. The framework also includes specific provisions for projects under tied aid arrangements and those aimed at strengthening national defense capabilities.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to improve the efficiency and transparency of managing foreign-funded public investment projects in Ukraine. By standardizing the procedures for loan acquisition and project monitoring, the government aims to secure more favorable financing terms and ensure better oversight of project implementation.

policydecision_details: Implemented measures to support agricultural production for the 2026-27 campaign in response to El Niño-related drought risks. The government is providing agricultural inputs, including seeds for beans, cassava, sweet potatoes, and short-cycle maize, to local farmers. Additionally, the province is promoting the expansion of fish production as a strategic alternative to mitigate potential crop losses. These efforts are supported by the maintenance of water storage levels in the Pequenos Libombos and Corumana dams, which are currently above 80% capacity.
contextoradditionalinfo: Meteorological forecasts from the National Meteorology Institute (INAM) indicate that the 2026-27 agricultural campaign will be significantly affected by the El Niño phenomenon, which is characterized by rainfall deficits. This follows a previous season that was severely impacted by heavy rainfall and flooding, necessitating proactive measures to ensure food availability and market supply in the Maputo Province.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Agriculture, Environment and Fisheries

policydecision_details: The Government of Mozambique has intensified crackdowns on illegal fishing, particularly in the Cahora Bassa Reservoir, by deploying a joint security task force. This initiative aims to reinforce inspection protocols and restore order to protect natural resources. The government has declared zero tolerance for smuggling and illicit activities that threaten the sustainability of strategic value chains. Authorities are also pursuing criminal accountability for individuals financing illegal operations to ensure the long-term viability of the sector.
contextoradditionalinfo: The intervention was prompted by a severe depletion of natural resources, specifically the collapse of kapenta stocks and the closure of commercial fisheries and cashew processing plants. These economic losses have threatened the sustainability of natural resources and strategic value chains essential to the national economy. The government identified that illegal activities and smuggling were the primary drivers of this resource depletion.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Agriculture, Environment, and Fisheries

policydecision_details: The Zambian government is set to sign an agreement with the United States to secure US$1.5 billion in funding for the national health sector over a five-year period. Zambia has committed to contributing an additional US$2.1 billion to the sector during the same timeframe. The agreement follows complex negotiations regarding data-sharing requirements, which were ultimately limited to monitoring and evaluating the funded programs. A controversial clause requiring the provision of biological samples was removed from the final deal. The funding is intended to support public health initiatives, including HIV/AIDS and malaria programs.
contextoradditionalinfo: The agreement is part of a new approach to foreign assistance by the United States, which encourages recipient countries to transition toward self-sufficient financing models. Negotiations were initially stalled due to concerns over American demands for access to medical data, a point of contention that has affected similar agreements in other African nations. The Zambian government clarified that the health funding is not linked to any arrangements regarding critical mineral resources.

policydecision_details: The Bank of Mozambique is implementing new measures to enhance transparency in the foreign exchange market and stimulate domestic production. Key actions include the introduction of a real-time monitoring platform for the foreign exchange market and a new financing mechanism for strategic sectors. The Monetary Policy Committee has approved a temporary mandatory reserve requirement regime that allows credit institutions to deduct new loans for import substitution and export expansion from their reserve requirements. Additionally, a monitoring center for international bank card usage has been established to improve financial oversight. These reforms aim to reduce information asymmetries and provide better predictability for business planning and investment.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Mozambican economy remains exposed to internal and external shocks, which have constrained economic activity, heightened uncertainty, and limited investment capacity. The Bank of Mozambique identified information asymmetries and operational incongruities in the current foreign exchange market that hinder business planning and import costs. By facilitating financing for import substitution and export growth, the central bank seeks to mitigate these constraints and support sustainable economic growth.

policydecision_details: The Mozambican government has introduced the Public Financial Management Strategy (EGFP) 2026–2035 to enhance transparency and accountability in public finance. The reform mandates regular disclosure of financial data, including public debt, budget execution, and investment results. Key measures include the creation of a public accounts disclosure calendar and the establishment of a Court of Auditors to oversee expenditure legality. The government aims to modernize the State Financial Administration System (e-SISTAFE) and improve public understanding of government accounts through simplified reporting. These efforts are designed to increase citizen participation and strengthen oversight of public resources.
contextoradditionalinfo: The strategy was developed to address the need for greater transparency and accountability in the management of public funds. By implementing these reforms, the government seeks to improve its Open Budget Index score and ensure that public expenditure is subject to rigorous scrutiny by oversight bodies and the public.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Hungary is initiating a comprehensive overhaul of its energy industry to address the country's high electricity costs. The strategy focuses on achieving energy sovereignty by reducing reliance on natural gas and crude oil imports. Key measures include extending the operational lifetime of existing nuclear power units and lifting the investment ban on wind power. Additionally, the government plans to enhance solar energy efficiency through the integration of new storage facilities.
contextoradditionalinfo: Hungary currently faces some of the highest electricity costs in Europe, prompting the government to seek structural changes to its energy sector. The overhaul is designed to improve energy security and reduce the economic burden of energy imports on the national economy.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: The Asian Development Bank has reaffirmed its commitment to support Cambodia's green economic development and climate resilience. The Ministry of Environment and the ADB will collaborate on projects involving reforestation, waste management, and the conservation of natural protected areas. Specific initiatives include supporting crab stock and mangrove forest conservation in coastal regions to improve local livelihoods. Additionally, the parties are working to develop a transparent carbon credit market to help Cambodia achieve carbon neutrality by 2050.
contextoradditionalinfo: This commitment aligns with the Royal Government of Cambodia's Pentagonal Strategy and the Ministry of Environment's Circular Strategy on Environment. The collaboration aims to address the global challenge of climate change while promoting environmental sustainability and socio-economic development.
beneficiaries: communities in natural protected areas, coastal communities
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: The New Zealand government is proposing updates to the 'Simply Safe & Suitable' food control plan template to simplify food safety obligations for businesses. The changes aim to reduce paperwork and focus on risk-based outcomes rather than complex administrative requirements. The proposal includes clearer guidance on managing food safety risks and reducing duplication in record-keeping. Additionally, officials are working on replacing periodic registration renewals with an ongoing registration process for certain businesses. Consultation on these changes is open until November 15, 2026.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of a broader government initiative to cut red tape and reduce unnecessary complexity for food businesses. By making food safety rules easier to understand and apply, the government intends to help businesses focus on delivering safe food to consumers more efficiently. This follows feedback from businesses requesting more outcome-focused and simplified regulatory requirements.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The 'Small Hydropower Plant' JSC has issued a call for competition for a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) project to construct the Dangi small hydropower plant. The project, initiated by 'Satellite-2005' JSC, involves building a 13.6 MW capacity facility in the Osh region. This initiative aims to enhance renewable energy infrastructure and stabilize electricity supply in the southern regions of Kyrgyzstan. Interested parties have 30 days from the publication date to submit their proposals for participation.
contextoradditionalinfo: The project is designed to address energy shortages in the southern regions of the Kyrgyz Republic by creating a modern, stable renewable energy source. It reflects the government's strategy to leverage private sector investment for critical infrastructure development.
decision_making_institution: National Investment Agency of the Kyrgyz Republic
beneficiaries: southern regions of the Kyrgyz Republic
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Negotiated a 1,350 per litre ceiling on the ex-gantry or landing cost of petrol to mitigate price volatility. This mechanism is designed to allow refiners and importers to absorb temporary cost increases and recover differences when market conditions improve. The ceiling will be reviewed monthly and published to ensure transparency. Additionally, the government is implementing a 30-day margin discount on petrol for public transporters and considering an excess profit tax on energy operators to fund transport support for vulnerable earners.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy aims to shield Nigerians from sharp fluctuations in global crude prices and exchange rates, which have caused significant uncertainty in transport fares and the prices of goods and services. The government seeks to provide targeted relief without returning to a blanket fuel subsidy, which it argues would impose unsustainable pressure on public finances.

policydecision_details: The Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) has successfully raised 3.39 billion cedis ($288.02 million) through a short-term domestic debt issuance. This capital injection is specifically intended to provide the necessary liquidity for the regulator to increase its purchasing capacity from local cocoa farmers. By securing these funds, COCOBOD aims to ensure that farmers are paid promptly for their produce during the harvest season. This measure serves to stabilize the income of cocoa producers and maintain the operational efficiency of the cocoa supply chain.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Ghana Cocoa Board frequently relies on domestic and international financing to manage the seasonal purchase of cocoa beans from farmers. This specific debt issuance was conducted on the domestic market to address immediate liquidity needs for the upcoming purchasing cycle, ensuring that the regulator can meet its obligations to farmers.

policydecision_details: Announced a series of measures to strengthen the asylum system and border management. These measures include enhancing biometric screening, accelerating the adjudication of asylum applications, and improving information-sharing between law enforcement and migration agencies. The government plans to relocate Refugee Reception Offices from inland areas to border regions to process applications closer to points of entry. Additionally, the Special Investigating Unit will be tasked with investigating fraudulent asylum status issuance to ensure the integrity of the system.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Greece is advancing major energy projects, including exploratory drilling in Block 2 of the Ionian Sea scheduled for April 2027 by a consortium of Energean, Exxon Mobil, and Helleniq Energy. The project aims to determine the commercial viability of natural gas or oil deposits at the Asopos 1 target. Additionally, the government is progressing with the Greece-Cyprus electricity interconnection and the Vertical Natural Gas Corridor to strengthen regional energy networks. These initiatives are part of a broader strategy to establish Greece as a key energy hub and enhance energy security. Long-term infrastructure development, including carbon dioxide storage at the Prinos field, is also underway to support industrial decarbonization.
