policydecision_details: Promoted investment in mango production to reduce reliance on imports, increase domestic production, and strengthen the crop’s economic value chain. The country currently imports around 46,211 tonnes of mangoes annually, valued at approximately OMR18.7 million, while domestic production exceeded 17,123 tonnes in 2025. The 2026–2030 localization plan aims to expand cultivated area to around 10,300 feddans and increase production to nearly 44,785 tonnes, supported by improved productivity, water-use efficiency, modern irrigation, better varieties, and agricultural research. The initiative also seeks to develop activities across the value chain, including nurseries, packaging, storage, logistics, processing, and marketing, creating opportunities for private investment, SMEs, employment, and food security.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

policydecision_details: Mozambique and Tanzania have signed a bilateral agreement to foster collaboration in the cashew sector. The agreement focuses on research and development, technology transfer, and the sharing of improved cashew varieties. Both countries aim to enhance cashew marketing, trade, and quality control standards to improve regional competitiveness. This framework is designed to support the growth of the cashew industry and increase value-addition through improved processing capacities.
contextoradditionalinfo: The agreement follows years of regional engagement and discussions among stakeholders to address common challenges in the East African cashew industry. Both countries are seeking to increase production and productivity while strengthening domestic processing to generate greater economic benefits. The collaboration is seen as a strategic step to build a more resilient and sustainable industry that supports the livelihoods of millions of smallholder farmers.
decision_making_institution: Instituto de Amêndoas de Moçambique IP (IAM) and Cashew nuts Board of Tanzania (CBT)

policydecision_details: Launched a Green Artificial Intelligence Alliance to promote the use of renewable and low-emission energy in artificial intelligence and high-performance computing. The initiative brings together government entities, private-sector companies, academic and research institutions, and investors to develop a national ecosystem for sustainable AI. Its 2026 work plan includes supporting research on energy-efficient computing, building national expertise, encouraging private-sector adoption of green technologies, and developing incentives for investment in clean digital solutions. The alliance supports Oman Vision 2040 by linking digital transformation and AI development with environmental sustainability, renewable energy, and economic development.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Transport, Communications and Information Technology

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture and the Palestinian Standards and Metrology Institution signed a technical cooperation agreement to implement a training and capacity-building programme on the Palestinian Good Agricultural Practices system (PAL-GAP – PS 4109). The programme will train 50 agricultural engineers from the Ministry as assistant advisors in applying good agricultural practices, with theoretical and practical training covering quality standards, certification requirements, and field implementation. Funded by the World Bank under the Social Recovery and Job Creation in Agriculture project, the initiative aims to improve the quality and competitiveness of Palestinian agricultural products, strengthen food safety and standards, and support access to export markets, particularly for products such as dates and olive oil.

Launched a pilot electronic system for managing employee leave and personnel movements as part of its digital transformation efforts. Developed by the Ministry’s Electronic Computing Department, the system digitises leave requests, study leave, ministry orders, training courses, official movement permits, and other administrative procedures, reducing paper-based transactions and improving data management and monitoring. The pilot phase will assess the system’s efficiency, identify and address issues, and support a potential rollout across other Ministry departments and units.

Approved an amendment allowing crude oil exports to Türkiye of up to 33,000 barrels per day as an initial stage, linked to the financing mechanism of the bilateral water framework agreement between the two countries. The decision connects Iraq’s oil export revenues with the financing of water-related cooperation and infrastructure under the agreement.

Supplied two electronic milking systems to model sheep farms in Yatta, Hebron, and Masafer Bani Na'im, at a total cost of approximately NIS 945,000 under the Sustainable Livestock Development Programme. The systems will support small-ruminant breed improvement by providing accurate milk-production data, updating farm records electronically, and improving herd and feeding management. The initiative aims to increase livestock productivity, reduce the time, effort, and costs associated with milking, support genetic selection and breeding programmes, improve the quality of animal products, and strengthen farmers’ resilience and sustainable livestock production.

Signed an agreement to construct an integrated fishing port in Mahout, Al Wusta Governorate, to strengthen the fisheries sector and support investment and local economic development. The project will improve fish landing, handling, marketing, storage, and processing facilities, while providing services for fishermen and creating opportunities for fish-processing industries, tourism, and maritime activities. The port will include breakwaters, berths, floating pontoons, a fish market, ice plants, vessel repair workshops, fishermen’s facilities, fish-processing plots, and supporting electricity, water, sewage, and road infrastructure. Given Mahout’s major role in the governorate’s fishing activity, the project is expected to increase the added value of fisheries products, support local communities, and contribute to the diversification and sustainable development of Oman’s fisheries economy.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation (Egypt) and the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) signed cooperation agreements to develop a master plan for agricultural and rural development in South Sinai and establish a strategic framework for Egypt’s olive value chain. The South Sinai initiative will focus on empowering local communities, particularly youth and women, creating sustainable livelihoods, improving the use of natural resources, and integrating local production into agricultural and food value chains. The olive-sector framework will assess the value chain from production and processing to marketing and consumption, identifying opportunities to increase productivity and competitiveness and inform a national strategy for sustainable growth and food security.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture and FAO signed 13 investment support agreements under the 18th round of the MAP II programme, supporting market-oriented agricultural investments, innovation, and the development of a sustainable food system across six Palestinian governorates. The projects represent a total investment of approximately NIS 4.35 million, with NIS 2.03 million provided by the programme and NIS 2.32 million contributed by beneficiaries. Supported activities include crop and livestock production, grain and animal feed production, food processing, packaging, and energy and water projects, selected based on their productivity, quality, and sustainability. The programme also supports Palestinian farmers and agricultural production amid the destruction and targeting of land, people, and water, contributing to food and water security and farmers’ resilience.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Launched a programme to install solar photovoltaic systems at public buildings operated by municipalities, expanding the use of renewable energy and improving energy efficiency across the Kingdom. The programme targets 104 municipalities and 188 municipal buildings, with a combined capacity of up to 3.4 MW, expected to reduce municipal electricity costs by around JD550,000 annually and cut carbon emissions by approximately 3,838 tonnes per year. It also includes specialised training for more than 550 municipal employees to strengthen local capacity for the operation and maintenance of the systems and ensure their long-term sustainability. The initiative supports Jordan’s energy transition, reduces the financial burden on municipalities, and promotes more sustainable local public services.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Launched a SAR 3.5 million project to improve urban water systems in Taiz, in partnership with Selah Foundation for Development. The project will strengthen the institutional and technical capacity of the local water and sanitation corporation, improve asset management and operation and maintenance, and reduce water losses. Together with a complementary French-funded project, the initiatives total SAR 7.4 million and are expected to directly benefit more than 139,000 people and indirectly benefit over 242,000, while improving the resilience of urban water infrastructure to climate-change impacts. The project forms part of SDRPY’s wider water-sector and development support across Yemen.
decision_making_institution: Saudi Development and Reconstruction Program for Yemen (SDRPY)

policydecision_details: Qatar and Guyana signed a memorandum of understanding to strengthen cooperation in agriculture and technology, covering crops, livestock, and fisheries. The agreement provides for the exchange of expertise, training, capacity building, and modern agricultural technologies, with the aim of supporting sustainable agricultural development and improving food security and supply chains. It also seeks to diversify food supply sources and create new opportunities for investment and cooperation between the two countries.

Iraq and Brazil agreed to proceed with signing memoranda of understanding (MoUs) covering livestock and crop production, following discussions on expanding agricultural cooperation. The talks focused particularly on developing Iraq’s poultry sector and strengthening broader cooperation in agricultural production. The agreement is expected to provide a framework for closer technical and sectoral collaboration between the two countries.

Supplied the sheep farm at Beit Qad Agricultural Research Station in Jenin with modern equipment and technologies worth approximately NIS 822,150 under the Sustainable Livestock Development Programme. The equipment includes electronic animal identification and herd data-management systems, feeding and livestock-production equipment, and specialized technologies to support genetic improvement and the production and preservation of improved genetic material. The initiative aims to improve herd management, milking and production efficiency, strengthen the station’s research and genetic improvement capacity, and support livestock productivity, food security, and the resilience of farmers and livestock breeders.

Signed a memorandum of understanding with Nutanix to explore the modernization of the Ministry’s digital infrastructure through hybrid multicloud technologies and artificial intelligence. The cooperation aims to strengthen business continuity, disaster recovery, cybersecurity, and the secure management of applications and data across different cloud environments. It also includes knowledge transfer and development of national technical skills, supporting the localization of advanced technology and MEWA’s broader digital transformation efforts.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

policydecision_details: Began compensating farmers and livestock breeders affected by recent agricultural fires triggered by El Niño, starting in Jijel with the distribution of livestock to affected breeders. The compensation programme will extend to all affected provinces and aims to restore agricultural activity as quickly as possible. Support includes the distribution of cattle, sheep, goats, and fodder, while specialized agricultural companies are rehabilitating damaged production infrastructure such as stables and poultry houses. Compensation will cover losses identified by local assessment committees, including livestock, production facilities, irrigation networks, beehives, and poultry houses, helping affected producers resume agricultural activities and rebuild their livelihoods.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Fisheries

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture and Ministry of Labour, through the Palestinian Employment Fund, signed agricultural grant agreements for 9 beneficiaries under the second phase of the SANIT project – Supporting the Agricultural and Food Cooperation Network in Palestine, with total grants of NIS 235,000. The grants target the fodder and plum sectors and aim to support sustainable agricultural businesses, strengthen agricultural value chains, create employment opportunities, increase production, and improve food security. Beneficiaries were selected through a competitive technical process based on project feasibility, sustainability, environmental impact, job creation, innovation, market access, and cooperative participation. The initiative also provides beneficiaries with agricultural extension and technical support to improve the productivity and long-term sustainability of their projects.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Ministry of Labour

policydecision_details: Launched the “Buthra” (Seed) initiative, a project aimed at economically empowering rural women and strengthening their role in agricultural and rural development. The initiative targets 520 vulnerable women through vocational training, support for small productive projects, and improved access to markets for rural products, helping increase income opportunities, improve livelihoods, and strengthen food security. The project also supports the development of sustainable rural enterprises and creates a more enabling environment for women to turn their productive skills into sustainable economic opportunities.

Launched the rehabilitation and development of the Al-Jalaa date palm farm in the Al-Bukamal area, in partnership with the Relief American Fund. The project covers approximately 2,000 dunums and around 12,000 date palms across 25 varieties, with planned improvements including fertilization and pest control, irrigation and infrastructure rehabilitation, solar energy, planting new offshoots, and agricultural training and knowledge transfer. The project also includes developing facilities for agritourism and related services, helping increase the farm’s economic value and support the development of the date palm sector in the area.

Launched the National Livestock Vaccination Project for the 2026/2027 season in North Al Batinah Governorate, targeting more than 500,000 livestock through six veterinary clinics and two mobile veterinary clinics. The programme aims to strengthen animal health, prevent livestock diseases, improve veterinary services, and support sustainable animal production and food security. Building on the previous season, when more than 900,000 vaccine doses were administered to over 449,000 livestock, the new programme will expand vaccination coverage to more than 70% of the governorate’s livestock population. A new digital vaccination platform will also improve field monitoring, data management, performance tracking, and decision-making.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

policydecision_details: Directed the implementation of a Cairo greening project to transform spaces cleared through urban redevelopment into green areas, alongside the restoration of historic and Islamic Cairo and the upgrading of infrastructure around heritage sites. The initiative aims to increase urban greenery, improve the capital’s environment, and enhance the use and attractiveness of historic areas through integrated heritage and tourism development. The government targets increasing the per-capita share of urban green space to 3 square metres by 2030, while the project is also linked to broader efforts to restore Cairo’s historic landmarks and improve the use of public and heritage spaces.

Launched the Water Regulation Forum as an international platform to strengthen cooperation among water-sector regulators and promote more adaptive, efficient, and sustainable regulatory frameworks. The forum will bring together regulators, policymakers, financial and international institutions, and water-sector experts to address challenges such as water scarcity, climate change, desalination, water reuse, investment, and digital transformation. Drawing on Saudi Arabia’s experience in managing one of the world’s largest integrated water systems, the initiative will facilitate knowledge exchange, compare regulatory approaches, and develop practices that can improve water-sector resilience, efficiency, service quality, and investment. The forum will also establish the Water Regulation Exchange (WREx) as a future annual platform for international regulatory cooperation and knowledge sharing.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Three UAE-backed solar power plants were inaugurated in Comoros, with a combined capacity of approximately 20 MW, supported by battery storage and new transmission infrastructure. The project, financed by ADFD and implemented by Masdar, aims to strengthen electricity infrastructure, reduce the country’s heavy dependence on imported diesel, improve power reliability, and expand access to renewable energy. The facilities are expected to generate around 33.75 GWh of clean electricity annually, support energy and economic resilience, and reduce carbon emissions while contributing to the country’s transition toward a more sustainable energy system.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Released 400,000 common carp fingerlings into water bodies in Nineveh as part of the One Million Fingerlings Project. The initiative aims to increase fish stocks, support fishermen, develop the fisheries sector, promote sustainable agricultural and livestock activities, and strengthen national food security.

policy_description: Seed technology and quality assurance systems
policydecision_details: Two new seed purification and processing lines were inaugurated at the Ahlelah facility in Nineveh, increasing total processing capacity to 30 tonnes per hour. The expansion, implemented by the World Bank emergency loan project team in coordination with the Ministry of Agriculture, also includes 11 new storage units to increase wheat storage capacity. The initiative supports the development of Iraq’s seed sector, strengthens wheat storage and processing infrastructure, and enhances agricultural production capacity.
policycategory: Seed technology and quality assurance systems

policydecision_details: Implemented a national livestock vaccination campaign against major animal diseases, including brucellosis, foot-and-mouth disease, and PPR, through veterinary directorates and departments across several governorates. More than 4,600 livestock have been vaccinated against brucellosis, alongside additional vaccinations against foot-and-mouth disease and PPR, as veterinary teams continue reaching targeted herds and livestock breeders. The campaign aims to strengthen disease prevention and control, protect livestock health and production, support farmers’ livelihoods, and contribute to national food security.

Launched preparations for the 2026 olive harvest campaign in partnership with national and international institutions to support farmers, strengthen their resilience, and protect agricultural land. The campaign will coordinate field interventions, volunteers, and supporting organizations, with decentralized committees established in each town to organize harvesting activities and provide assistance to farmers in areas most in need. The initiative also aims to facilitate farmers’ access to their land and protect the olive harvest amid ongoing challenges and attacks against farmers and their property, while strengthening the resilience of the agricultural sector and its contribution to the national economy.

Supported agricultural marketing and strengthening the presence of local dates in regional markets. The seasonal market, organized and supervised by the Ministry’s Al-Mithnab office, brings together producers, marketers, and buyers through organized sales and auctions covering more than 70 date varieties. The Ministry also monitors incoming dates, ensures compliance with regulations and quality requirements, and provides an organized marketing environment that supports farmers, marketers, and consumers.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

policydecision_details: Signed a cooperation agreement to launch a two-year Poultry Farm Biosecurity Programme aimed at strengthening disease prevention, surveillance, hygiene, and biosecurity practices at poultry farms. The programme will build the capacity of agricultural, livestock, animal health, and poultry-sector personnel, helping improve production efficiency, protect animal health, and strengthen food security in Abu Dhabi.
decision_making_institution: Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

policydecision_details: Launched an A-to-E Food Label Verification System to assess the accuracy of nutritional information displayed on packaged food products. The service tests whether declared levels of sugar, fat, calories, protein, carbohydrates, fibre, and sodium match the actual contents of products. The classification is intended to help food businesses validate nutritional claims, support regulatory compliance, and strengthen consumer confidence in food labelling. An A grade indicates accuracy of the nutritional information, not that the product is healthier.

Distributed two fodder seed production units to agricultural associations in Al-Burj and Surif to support more than 50 farmers directly and around 3,000 people indirectly. Funded by the European Union and the Palestinian government, the initiative provides agricultural machinery and seeds to reduce production costs, improve productivity, strengthen livestock production, and enhance the resilience and livelihoods of farming communities in Area C.

Developed an integrated logistics hub centred on Dakhla Atlantique, connecting the future port with the El Argoub logistics zone and the El Guerguerat trade corridor to strengthen trade links with Mauritania and sub-Saharan Africa. The USD 1.6 billion port, expected to begin operations in 2029, will have an annual capacity of 35 million tonnes and will be supported by a 1,650-hectare industrial zone. The integrated network is intended to improve logistics connectivity, facilitate trade, and position Dakhla as a regional gateway, although attracting shipping lines and maintaining competitive transport costs remain key challenges.

Signed a memorandum of understanding with AMKM (UAE) and Aqua Bridge Holding to explore investment and development opportunities in the blue economy, aquaculture, sustainable fisheries, marine and freshwater resources, and food security. The cooperation covers developing fish hatcheries and farms, processing and cold-chain infrastructure, feasibility studies, advanced technologies, and international best practices to support sustainable use of water resources, economic development, and food security.

Developed a 200,000-ton grain storage silo project to establish a strategic reserve of essential commodities, including wheat, barley, corn, and soybeans, while increasing the port’s capacity to receive and handle grain shipments. The project includes 20 silos, grain-handling equipment, an electrical substation, and supporting facilities, and is expected to strengthen food supply security, improve grain logistics, and create 200–300 jobs once operational.

policy_description: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
policydecision_details: Launched an Integrated Digital Environmental Impact Assessment (IDEIA) system to streamline environmental approvals, reduce paperwork, and speed up investment procedures while maintaining environmental standards. The platform allows investors and consultants to submit and track environmental studies electronically, while enabling the Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) to manage reviews and approvals through a central database. The initiative also supports Egypt’s green industrial transition, digital transformation, carbon compliance, and improved competitiveness of Egyptian industries and exports.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Environment, the Ministry of Investment and Foreign Trade
policycategory: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources

policydecision_details: Signed agreements worth OMR1.19 million to restore and maintain 64 aflaj damaged by the recent low-pressure weather system in North Al Batinah. The programme covers 76 aflaj in total and aims to protect these vital water systems, supporting agricultural activity, local communities, and sustainable water management.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Integrated its green hydrogen programme with a broader industrial ecosystem linking renewable energy, battery storage, green manufacturing, and exports. The approach aims to use solar and wind power with energy storage to provide reliable electricity for industries such as green ammonia, low-carbon fuels, iron and steel, while developing higher-value products for international markets. Hydrom is also focusing on stronger project frameworks, local capabilities, engineering capacity, and digital technologies to support commercially viable hydrogen and renewable energy projects.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Energy and Minerals
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Indian customs authorities have launched an investigation into a significant surge in soybean imports declared as originating from Niger. The probe focuses on suspicions that these shipments are actually sourced from Nigeria and mislabelled to circumvent import tariffs. Importers are now required to provide additional documentation to verify the true origin of the soybeans. Failure to prove the origin could result in the application of a 45% import tariff on the shipments.
contextoradditionalinfo: India allows duty-free imports of soybeans from least-developed countries like Niger. However, imports from Niger surged to 380,868 metric tonnes in the first seven months of 2026, despite the country's annual production being less than 100 tonnes. This discrepancy led authorities to suspect illegal relabelling of Nigerian soybeans to avoid the standard 45% import duty.

policydecision_details: Signed a memorandum of understanding with Al-Abbar Company, with the participation of the Agricultural Cooperative Bank, to provide farmers with agricultural machinery, equipment, and related tools through flexible installment plans. The initiative aims to modernize agricultural operations, improve production efficiency, reduce farmers’ financial burden, and promote the use of modern technologies to support sustainable agriculture and food security.

Signed an agreement with Relief American Fund to rehabilitate and develop the Al-Jalaa date palm farm in Al-Bukamal. The project will improve irrigation, pest and fertilizer management, and farm infrastructure, while introducing solar energy, expanding palm cultivation, and providing training and knowledge transfer. It also includes developing agricultural tourism facilities to increase the farm’s economic value and support the date palm sector in the area.

Suspended foreign grape imports during the domestic harvest season to support local growers and improve the marketing of locally produced grapes. With production in Duhok expected to increase significantly, the measure is complemented by efforts to expand distribution to other Iraqi provinces and increase grape-processing capacity to manage surplus production and reduce post-harvest losses.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Water Resources

policydecision_details: Launched an AI-powered Smart Voice Assistant for its Nama e-services platform, allowing users to access government services through natural voice commands and receive tailored information on requirements and procedures. The initiative supports Saudi Arabia’s digital transformation by improving service accessibility, reducing the time and effort required to access services, and using data and AI to enhance service delivery and decision-making.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture signed a memorandum of understanding with Saudi and Syrian private-sector groups to study and develop Syria’s poultry industry and related value chains. The agreement covers the rehabilitation and expansion of poultry farms, hatcheries and slaughterhouses, development of integrated egg and broiler production complexes, food processing, cold storage, marketing and export. It also addresses biosecurity, veterinary health and modern technologies, with the aim of increasing production, improving efficiency and quality, strengthening competitiveness, and opening regional and international markets for Syrian poultry products.
source1name: Syrian Ministry of Agriculture and Agrarian

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture signed a memorandum of understanding with Al-Khatib Company to provide farmers with agricultural machinery and equipment through flexible instalment plans, in coordination with the Agricultural Cooperative Bank. The initiative aims to improve farmers’ access to production equipment, increase agricultural productivity and operational efficiency, reduce costs, and strengthen the competitiveness of agricultural products, supporting sustainable agricultural and economic development.

The Ministry of Agriculture signed a memorandum of understanding with Khair Al-Jiyad Cheese Factory to study establishing an integrated project for feed production and dairy processing. The proposed project would cultivate up to 5,000 hectares of fodder crops using modern center-pivot and linear irrigation systems, linked to feed mills, storage and logistics facilities, dairy farms, and cheese and dairy-processing plants. The project aims to improve resource and water-use efficiency, secure feed supplies for livestock, strengthen local agricultural and dairy value chains, and support sustainable agricultural and food production.
source1name: Syrian Ministry of Agriculture and Agrarian Reform

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture and FAO signed a cooperation agreement under the Building Resilience to Cope with Climate Change in Jordan through Improving Water Use Efficiency in the Agriculture Sector (BRCCJ) project to strengthen farmers’ capacity to adapt to climate change through climate-smart farmer field schools and promote water-saving agricultural technologies. The Green Climate Fund-supported project will establish 44 farmer field schools and 44 field days in Madaba, Karak, Tafileh, and Maan, benefiting around 880 farmers, while preparing the groundwork for additional field schools. The initiative builds on previous training of agricultural extension officers and aims to improve water-use efficiency, strengthen food and water security, and build a more climate-resilient agricultural sector in areas affected by water scarcity and climate change.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: The ministry signed a technical, scientific, and technological cooperation agreement with the Arab Center for the Studies of Arid Zones and Dry Lands (ACSAD), along with three memoranda of understanding focused on strengthening Iraq’s agricultural sector and addressing desertification. The agreements cover the development of the seed sector, the adoption of salt-tolerant crop varieties, and the introduction of crops better suited to Iraq’s environmental and climatic conditions, with the aim of increasing agricultural productivity, improving crop efficiency, and promoting more sustainable farming systems.

The Agricultural Extension and Training Directorate, in cooperation with ACSAD, launched an advanced training programme on irrigation water management using modern technologies. The training focuses on practical crop modelling through AquaCrop, analysis of satellite data using Google Earth Engine, and remote sensing applications to strengthen the capacity of agricultural staff to manage water scarcity and salinity more efficiently. The initiative aims to improve irrigation and crop water-use efficiency, support sustainable management of water and agricultural resources, and strengthen Arab cooperation and knowledge transfer in response to Iraq’s water-related challenges.

The Ministry of Economic Affairs and Development signed a €35 million financial cooperation agreement with Germany, including funding to strengthen technical and vocational training and support coastal biodiversity conservation and the blue economy. The coastal component will focus on protecting ecosystems, sustainable natural-resource management, marine research, reducing marine waste and overfishing, and addressing the impacts of climate change and coastal erosion.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Economic Affairs and Development

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture, in partnership with the Arab Center for the Studies of Arid Zones and Dry Lands (ACSAD), launched an advanced training programme on irrigation water management using modern technologies, including AquaCrop crop simulation, Google Earth Engine, and remote sensing. The programme aims to strengthen agricultural staff capacity to improve irrigation efficiency and address water scarcity and salinity challenges.

The Ministry of Agriculture, in partnership with UNDP, the Council for Development and Reconstruction, and the World Bank, launched a US$18.5 million agricultural grant programme under the GATE project to support farmers, women farmers, cooperatives, and farmers’ associations. Grants will finance climate-smart investments including irrigation and water management, renewable energy, protected agriculture, machinery, post-harvest management, food safety, packaging, marketing, and rehabilitation of damaged agricultural facilities. The initiative aims to restore production affected by the recent war, strengthen farmers’ resilience and livelihoods, improve productivity and competitiveness, and support food security and sustainable agrifood sector recovery.

The Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation launched the distribution of 100 agricultural tractors to farmers at Al-Rahad Agricultural Scheme, supplied by Giad Company through the Agricultural Bank of Sudan, as part of efforts to improve agricultural productivity and address machinery and irrigation-related constraints. The ministry also reviewed challenges including electricity supply, bird pests, canal clearance, and silt accumulation, while emphasizing an approach that links agricultural finance with insurance, extension services, and value-chain financing. The ministry further highlighted the agricultural sector’s role in supporting reconstruction efforts in Kordofan and Darfur.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation / Agricultural Bank of Sudan

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture introduced an exceptional and temporary mechanism for the sanitary emergency cutting of completely dead forest trees affected by pests or diseases, aiming to prevent infestations from spreading to healthy trees and protect Lebanon’s forest resources. The measure is based on technical inspections and applies only to trees confirmed to be completely dead and posing a risk to forest health; living or partially dead trees are excluded. The mechanism requires strict supervision, documentation, and controls over the resulting wood, including on-site chipping or approved treatment before transport, with permits required for any movement and a ban on selling or storing untreated wood.

The General Organization for Seed Multiplication announced the sale of potato seed produced under the 2026 national autumn-season potato programme, with payment to be made at a later stage. The measure supports the availability of certified planting material and facilitates farmers’ access to potato seed for the upcoming autumn production season.

Italy has extended the deadline for taxpayers to exercise the right to deduct input VAT and record purchase invoices through Article 17 of Legislative Decree No. 148/2026. This measure allows taxpayers to deduct input VAT through the annual VAT return for the second year following the year in which the right arose. Additionally, Legislative Decree No. 10/2026 introduces a new VAT Consolidated Act effective from 1 January 2027. This reform involves a complete reorganization and renumbering of existing VAT provisions to modernize the legislative framework. Companies are required to update their internal systems, including VAT codes and ERP mappings, to align with these changes.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy aims to provide enhanced flexibility for input VAT recovery and to modernize the Italian VAT legislative framework. By extending the deduction deadlines, the government is restoring more favorable time limits that were previously in place before 2017. The introduction of the new VAT Consolidated Act serves to reorganize and renumber existing provisions to improve clarity and compliance.

policy_description: Seed technology and quality assurance systems
policydecision_details: The Seed Testing and Certification Directorate is strengthening technical oversight of seed cleaning and preparation facilities operated by seed-producing companies ahead of the upcoming agricultural season. The programme covers monitoring seed reception, cleaning, testing, certification, and the performance of cleaning lines to ensure compliance with approved technical standards. It also focuses on preserving the genetic purity, quality, and production characteristics of seed varieties, ensuring that farmers receive certified, high-quality planting material. The measures aim to improve agricultural inputs, raise productivity, support Iraqi farmers, and strengthen food security and sustainable agricultural production.
policycategory: Seed technology and quality assurance systems

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture launched a digital agricultural extension portal to strengthen direct communication between farmers, extension officers, and agricultural experts. The platform provides farmers with access to reliable technical advice, agricultural recommendations, and extension services, helping improve production efficiency, support informed decision-making, and accelerate access to services across Iraq’s governorates. The initiative forms part of the Ministry’s broader digital transformation efforts and aims to build a modern, technology-enabled agricultural extension system that supports sustainable agricultural development and food security.

The Ministry of Agriculture – Lebanon issued a clarification on the new fisheries and aquaculture law following consultations with fishermen, cooperatives, and unions. The ministry explained that industrial fishing is restricted to Lebanon’s exclusive economic zone and that the law expands Lebanese fishermen’s fishing rights within territorial waters from six to twelve nautical miles. It also clarified that the law does not establish that 30% of territorial waters are marine reserves and provides a legal framework for aquaculture, with implementing regulations being prepared to prioritise fishermen’s cooperatives and protect their economic interests.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Approved an energy escape clause for Greece, allowing the country to fund critical energy projects worth up to €1 billion by 2028. This decision permits Greece to exclude eligible energy expenditure from the EU framework's net primary expenditure growth limits. The policy aims to reduce energy costs, strengthen energy independence, and limit exposure to international crises. The government retains the flexibility to support households and businesses as needed while maintaining these investments.
contextoradditionalinfo: Greece sought this approval to navigate the EU's economic governance framework while addressing the need for energy infrastructure investment. The measure is designed to accelerate the transition away from fossil fuels and enhance the resilience of the European energy system. It reflects Greece's strategic objective to lower energy costs and improve its economic influence within the European Union.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: The Arab Organization for Agricultural Development (AOAD) launched a Capacity-Building Program for Sudan’s Agricultural Sector to strengthen the human, institutional, and organizational capacities of the country’s agriculture sector. The programme will provide technical support for agricultural policy development, institutional strengthening, natural resource management, production systems, and agricultural value chains. It also promotes technology transfer, digital transformation, climate-smart and precision agriculture, innovation, and evidence-based decision-making, while enhancing the skills of farmers, extension personnel, and agribusiness institutions to improve productivity, competitiveness, resilience, and sustainable agricultural development.
decision_making_institution: The Arab Organization for Agricultural Development (AOAD)

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture, with support from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), launched a national livestock vaccination campaign by receiving 1.5 million doses of foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) vaccine for cattle, alongside additional vaccines for sheep. The initiative aims to strengthen disease prevention and control, protect livestock from regional disease outbreaks, enhance veterinary surveillance and early detection, ensure safe vaccine distribution and quality control, and improve livestock health and food security through a comprehensive national immunization programme.

The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) and the Agricultural Credit Corporation (ACC) signed a cooperation agreement to strengthen sustainable agricultural financing in Jordan through the development of innovative blended finance mechanisms. The initiative aims to improve access to finance for smallholder farmers, women, youth, and agricultural SMEs, enhance the resilience of the agrifood sector to economic and climate-related challenges, and support agricultural development, food security, and rural livelihoods through closer collaboration between national and international institutions.

Intensified its compulsory Foot-and-Mouth Disease (FMD) vaccination program and tightened livestock movement controls to curb disease outbreaks. Farmers are required to contribute to a cost-recovery scheme for vaccines, while the government provides infrastructure and logistics. Authorities have warned against the illegal sale of government-procured vaccines by veterinary staff, threatening prosecution for those who sabotage the campaign. Movement of livestock is now strictly regulated, requiring official permits based on vaccination status to protect the national herd and international trade interests.
contextoradditionalinfo: Foot-and-Mouth Disease (FMD) poses a significant threat to Uganda's livestock industry and international trade, as affected countries restrict imports of animal products. The government initiated this policy shift to move away from reliance on the Consolidated Fund for vaccine supplies and to ensure the security of the national herd, which is vital for the dairy sector and the livelihoods of millions of people.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Industry and Fisheries (MAAIF)

policydecision_details: The Low Pay Commission has issued its 2026 recommendations for the National Minimum Wage in Ireland. The primary objective is to establish a wage rate that incentivizes work while remaining fair and sustainable for the economy. The recommendations aim to support as many workers as possible without causing significant adverse effects on national competitiveness or employment levels. This report provides a comprehensive analysis of the economic context, labour market statistics, and sectoral breakdowns to inform the wage setting process.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is driven by the need to balance the Minimum Essential Standard of Living (MESL) with the broader economic realities of the Irish labour market. The Commission evaluates various factors including GDP growth, job vacancy rates, and sectoral earnings to ensure the minimum wage remains an effective tool for poverty reduction and economic inclusion. The report serves as a formal advisory document to guide government policy on wage regulation for the year 2026.

policydecision_details: Approved the inclusion of a national project to restore and regulate the Nile River and its branches into the Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation’s budget for fiscal years 2026/2027 through 2028/2029. The project focuses on restoring the river's original watercourse by removing illegal encroachments, such as landfilling and unauthorized construction. It also involves creating updated digital topographic and bathymetric maps to monitor the riverbed and banks. Additionally, the project includes a comprehensive survey of public assets related to irrigation and drainage to ensure better infrastructure maintenance. This initiative aims to safeguard water structures and improve the management of water flow across the country.
contextoradditionalinfo: The project is designed to address long-standing issues of encroachment along the Nile, which obstruct water flow and threaten the integrity of irrigation infrastructure. By establishing a baseline of accurate data on the riverbed and banks, the government intends to improve the long-term management and development of the Nile's water resources, which are critical for Egypt's agricultural productivity and overall water security.

policydecision_details: The Taita Taveta County Forest Conservation and Management Bill, 2026, establishes a comprehensive legal and institutional framework for the sustainable management of forest resources within the county. It creates a Directorate and a Committee to oversee forest conservation, management plans, and community participation. The bill also introduces provisions for licensing, trade in forest products, and the establishment of urban parks and green zones. Furthermore, it outlines incentives for sustainable forestry practices and sets penalties for prohibited activities to ensure compliance.
contextoradditionalinfo: This legislation is introduced to give effect to the fourth schedule of the Constitution of Kenya regarding forestry, aiming to promote the development and sustainable management of forest resources for the socio-economic prosperity of Taita Taveta County.

policy_description: Anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, safeguard measures
policydecision_details: The U.S. Department of Commerce has initiated countervailing duty investigations regarding imports of truck bed covers from the People's Republic of China and India. This action follows a petition alleging that these imports are being unfairly subsidized and causing material injury to the domestic U.S. industry. The investigation will determine if these imports are subject to countervailing duties to offset the impact of foreign subsidies. The scope of the investigation covers various configurations of truck bed covers, including folding, roll-up, one-piece, and retractable models.
contextoradditionalinfo: The initiation of these investigations is part of the U.S. government's trade defense mechanism to address allegations of unfair trade practices. Petitioners have filed an allegation of critical circumstances, prompting the Department of Commerce to assess whether the imports are materially injuring or threatening material injury to the U.S. industry. The process involves coordination with the U.S. International Trade Commission to evaluate the economic impact on domestic producers.
beneficiaries: domestic manufacturers of truck bed covers
policycategory: Anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, safeguard measures

policydecision_details: The Taita Taveta County Water and Sanitation Services Bill, 2026, establishes a comprehensive legal and institutional framework for the provision of water and sanitation services within the county. It mandates the creation of County Water Service Providers and a dedicated Rural Water Service Provider to manage infrastructure and service delivery. The bill includes provisions for tariff regulation, sewerage management, and the establishment of a Taita Taveta Rural Water Fund. Furthermore, it outlines regulatory measures for borehole construction, rainwater harvesting, and the protection of water resources to ensure sustainable service delivery.
contextoradditionalinfo: This legislation is introduced to formalize the governance of water and sanitation services at the county level in Taita Taveta, Kenya. It aims to address challenges in service delivery, particularly in rural and underserved areas, by creating specialized entities and funds. The bill seeks to improve infrastructure management, ensure commercial viability of water services, and protect vital water resources through structured oversight and regulatory enforcement.
beneficiaries: rural households, urban residents of Taita Taveta

policydecision_details: The Taita Taveta County Animal Health and Livestock Movement Control Bill, 2026, establishes a comprehensive framework for the management of veterinary services and livestock movement within the county. It provides for the prevention, surveillance, and control of animal diseases and pests to ensure sustainable animal health. The bill mandates the creation of a County Veterinary Service, a Livestock Development Fund, and a Rangeland Inspectorate Unit to enforce regulations. Additionally, it introduces systems for animal identification and traceability to improve governance and disease management.
contextoradditionalinfo: The bill is introduced to address the need for effective veterinary governance and to mitigate the risks associated with animal diseases and pests in Taita Taveta County. By regulating livestock movement and establishing institutional oversight, the county aims to protect animal health and support the livestock sector's productivity.

policydecision_details: The Mozambican government has announced a new agribusiness incubation programme set to launch in 2026, targeting at least 1,000 entrepreneurs annually. The initiative aims to transform subsistence agriculture into professional, income-generating business activities. It will involve collaboration with the private sector and producer associations to provide necessary skills and capacity building. The government is also working with Gapi to facilitate improved access to credit for these producers.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy responds to the need to modernize the agricultural sector in Mozambique, moving away from subsistence farming toward market-oriented production. Stakeholders, including the National Federation of Peasant and Agricultural Producer Associations (FENAGRI), have identified high bureaucracy and limited access to financing as major barriers to growth. The program seeks to address these challenges by fostering specialized associativism and professionalizing agricultural value chains.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Agriculture, Environment and Fisheries

policydecision_details: The Government of Mozambique is updating its National Cybersecurity Strategy for the 2026–2030 period to implement the Cybersecurity Act. This strategy aims to translate legislative obligations into concrete initiatives, performance indicators, and monitoring mechanisms. It focuses on strengthening the protection of Critical Information Infrastructure across strategic sectors, including finance and public safety. The initiative seeks to transition the country from basic cybersecurity capabilities to a phase of greater institutional maturity, resilience, and digital trust.
contextoradditionalinfo: The update follows the enactment of the Cyber Security and Cybercrime Acts in June 2025, prompted by a significant rise in cyber incidents, with approximately 39,600 cases recorded in 2025. These incidents, particularly electronic payment and computer fraud, have threatened the continuity of essential services and the functioning of the economy. The strategy is designed to mitigate these risks by fostering a culture of cybersecurity and enhancing coordination between the state, academia, and the private sector.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Communications and Digital Transformation

policy_description: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget
policydecision_details: The Ministry of Finance of Ghana has issued the 2026 Budget Implementation Instructions to provide guidance to all Ministers, Chief Directors, and Heads of Covered Entities. This document serves as the operational framework for the implementation of the 2026 Budget and Economic Policy of the Government. It is issued pursuant to regulation 62 (1) of the Public Financial Management Regulations, 2019 (L.I. 2378). The instructions follow the passage of the Appropriation (No. 2) Act, 2025 (Act 1126) by Parliament and the subsequent presidential assent on 19th December 2025.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is a standard administrative procedure following the passage of the national budget act to ensure that government entities adhere to financial management regulations during the 2026 fiscal year.
policycategory: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget

policydecision_details: Announced a €16 million aid programme to support young adults with rental costs. The initiative provides a monthly subsidy of up to €300 for those renting apartments and €200 for those renting rooms. The programme is scheduled to run for the entirety of 2026 and 2027. It aims to assist approximately 2,300 individuals with a total potential benefit of €7,200 per person.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is designed as a 'historic call for aid' to address housing affordability challenges for young people in the Murcia region. It is intended to be accessible to Spanish nationals, EU citizens, and non-EU legal residents living in the area.

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: The National Consumer Commission (NCC) has launched the National Opt-Out Registry to provide consumers with a mechanism to block unwanted direct marketing communications. Empowered by the Consumer Protection Act Amendment Regulations of 2026, the registry requires direct marketers to register and cleanse their contact lists on a monthly basis. Consumers can use this system to pre-emptively block unwanted calls, SMSes, and electronic communications. The system is being phased in, with full functionality for consumers to block marketers expected by May 2027.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced in response to a significant surge in unsolicited direct marketing. According to the 2026 South Africa Spam Report, spam calls increased by 25.2% and spam SMSes by 58.9% compared to the previous year, leading to a high volume of unwanted communication for South African consumers.
decision_making_institution: Department of Trade, Industry and Competition
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection

policydecision_details: Mandated that all commercial banks reduce their nonperforming loan (NPL) ratio to 10% by December 2026. This regulatory requirement aims to improve asset quality and strengthen the balance sheets of the 23 banks operating in the country. Lenders are expected to enhance their credit risk management practices, including more thorough borrower assessments and improved debt recovery efforts. The central bank is also developing a new directive on credit risk management to provide clearer oversight of loan approvals and monitoring. This measure is intended to ensure that banks can effectively support productive economic activities while maintaining financial stability.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy follows a period of significant deterioration in banking sector asset quality, with NPLs rising from 15% in 2020 to 22% by December 2024. This trend was exacerbated by the economic crisis and the domestic debt exchange program launched in 2022, which negatively impacted bank profitability, liquidity, and solvency. By enforcing a 10% NPL target, the Bank of Ghana seeks to mitigate risks to the financial system and ensure that banks have the capacity to redirect resources toward new lending for businesses and households.

policy_description: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget
policydecision_details: The document provides the 2025 Programme Based Budgeting Estimates for the Ministry of Finance in Ghana. It outlines the financial planning and budgetary allocations for the fiscal year 2025. The document serves as a formal administrative record for the Ministry's operational and programmatic expenditures. It does not contain specific agricultural policy measures or commodity-level interventions.
contextoradditionalinfo: This document is a standard budgetary planning tool used by the Ghanaian government to manage public finances and departmental allocations for the 2025 fiscal year.
policycategory: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget

policydecision_details: NAFDAC has intensified enforcement actions against the circulation of banned, unregistered, and substandard pesticides across Nigeria. The agency has officially phased out specific active ingredients including paraquat, chlorpyrifos, and atrazine, with all phase-out periods concluding by January 1, 2026. Additionally, the importation, manufacture, and sale of 100 ml pack sizes of dichlorvos (DDVP) have been prohibited due to misuse concerns. NAFDAC is actively seizing illegal products and sealing unauthorized manufacturing facilities to protect public health and food safety. The agency is also strengthening collaboration with law enforcement to disrupt illegal supply chains.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to address the risks posed by the misuse of hazardous pesticides on agricultural produce and to curb the illegal movement of unregistered agrochemicals across borders. NAFDAC identified that banned products were entering local markets through unauthorized routes, necessitating a nationwide crackdown to ensure that only approved pesticides are used responsibly in agricultural production.
decision_making_institution: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)

policydecision_details: Signed a financing agreement with the French Ambassador to Uganda. The agreement secures 69 million euros in funding dedicated to the construction of water and sanitation infrastructure. This project aims to improve public health and living conditions through enhanced access to clean water and sanitation facilities. The investment represents a significant commitment to developing essential public utility infrastructure in the country.
contextoradditionalinfo: The agreement is part of ongoing efforts to improve national water and sanitation infrastructure, which is critical for public health and development. By securing international financing, the government aims to address gaps in service delivery and infrastructure coverage.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development

policydecision_details: The Medium Term Development Plan (2027-2030) serves as the strategic framework for Tuvalu's national development trajectory. It outlines the government's priorities for socioeconomic progress, establishing the overarching goals and planning horizon for the country's development initiatives during this period. The plan is designed to guide institutional efforts and coordinate national resources to achieve sustainable development outcomes, though specific implementation details, target groups, and budgetary allocations are not provided in the current documentation.
contextoradditionalinfo: This document represents the medium-term strategic planning instrument for the Government of Tuvalu, intended to guide national development efforts between 2027 and 2030.

country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
policydecision_details: The Organic Action Plan for England, developed by Defra in partnership with the English Organic Forum, serves as a strategic roadmap to increase the share of organic farmland and strengthen domestic supply chains. Its primary objectives are to remove barriers to growth, enhance market development for organic products, and improve consumer understanding of organic production methods. The plan focuses on three main themes: increasing and managing organic supply, realigning domestic supply and demand, and increasing consumer demand for English organic products. By supporting farmers in transitioning to organic practices, the framework aims to contribute to broader national goals, including nature recovery, soil health, biodiversity, and climate resilience. The implementation approach relies on a collaborative partnership between government and industry to ensure that organic farming is viewed as a productive, sustainable, and accessible choice for both producers and households across England.
contextoradditionalinfo: The plan addresses the stagnation in the share of England's farmland managed organically despite rising consumer demand, aiming to turn industry ambition into actionable growth while supporting the government's environmental and rural development objectives.

policydecision_details: The Master Plan 2025 (DMP 2025) is a strategic urban planning framework developed by the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) to guide Singapore's land use and development over the next 10 to 15 years. Based on the seven pillars of the Long-Term Plan, the framework focuses on four key themes aimed at creating a future where life's essentials are accessible, work-life harmony is prioritized, and heritage and nature are integrated into neighborhoods. The plan was developed through an extensive public engagement process involving approximately 220,000 participants since October 2023, utilizing exhibitions, focus group discussions, workshops, and ideas competitions to ensure community-driven development.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Master Plan 2025 is the latest iteration of Singapore's statutory land use plan, designed to shape the physical development of the nation through collaborative engagement with the public.

policydecision_details: The 2026-2028 Medium-Term Debt Management Strategy (MTDS) is a strategic borrowing framework developed by the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning (MFDP) and the Central Bank of Liberia (CBL) to manage the government's debt portfolio. Its primary objective is to meet financing needs and payment obligations at the lowest possible cost while maintaining a prudent level of risk. The strategy adopts an operational target of a 60:40 ratio between external and domestic financing, emphasizing the maintenance of external concessional financing while gradually deepening the domestic bond market. The scope of the strategy covers the central government's total debt, including both domestic and external obligations. The framework is designed to ensure debt sustainability in the medium term, given the country's moderate risk of debt distress for external debt and high risk for overall debt, by providing a structured approach to borrowing that aligns with macroeconomic assumptions, including projected GDP growth driven by mining, agriculture, and services.
contextoradditionalinfo: The 2026-2028 Medium-Term Debt Management Strategy (MTDS) is a strategic borrowing framework developed by the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning (MFDP) and the Central Bank of Liberia (CBL) to manage the government's debt portfolio. Its primary objective is to meet financing needs and payment obligations at the lowest possible cost while maintaining a prudent level of risk. The strategy adopts an operational target of a 60:40 ratio between external and domestic financing, emphasizing the maintenance of external concessional financing while gradually deepening the domestic bond market. The scope of the strategy covers the central government's total debt, including both domestic and external obligations. The framework is designed to ensure debt sustainability in the medium term, given the country's moderate risk of debt distress for external debt and high risk for overall debt, by providing a structured approach to borrowing that aligns with macroeconomic assumptions, including projected GDP growth driven by mining, agriculture, and services.

policy_description: Scheme "Restructuring of national science, technology and innovation programs" (2026-2035)
policydecision_details: The Scheme for the 'Restructuring of national science, technology and innovation programs' (2026-2035) establishes a comprehensive strategic framework aimed at modernizing and optimizing the national research and innovation landscape in Viet Nam. The primary objective is to enhance the efficiency and impact of national-level science and technology programs by aligning them with emerging global trends, national economic priorities, and the need for sustainable industrialization. The scope of the framework encompasses the reorganization of existing research programs, the prioritization of key technological sectors, and the strengthening of the interface between scientific research and practical application in the economy. It outlines institutional responsibilities for managing these programs, sets implementation priorities focused on high-tech development and digital transformation, and defines mechanisms for monitoring and evaluating the performance of scientific initiatives. The expected outcomes include a more robust national innovation system, increased technological competitiveness, and the effective integration of science and technology into the broader national development agenda.
contextoradditionalinfo: The programme is designed to address the need for structural economic transformation in Viet Nam by leveraging innovation and entrepreneurship as key drivers for sustainable growth.

policydecision_details: The National Innovation Startup Programme (2026–2035) establishes a long-term strategic vision for Viet Nam to accelerate the development of its national innovation ecosystem. The framework aims to enhance the capacity of startups and innovative enterprises by fostering a supportive environment for research, development, and commercialization of new technologies. It focuses on strengthening the linkages between academic institutions, research centers, and the private sector to drive economic growth and industrial competitiveness. The programme outlines priorities for improving the regulatory environment for startups, increasing access to venture capital and financial support, and promoting digital transformation across various sectors. By targeting entrepreneurs and innovative businesses, the strategy seeks to cultivate a culture of creativity and technological advancement, ultimately contributing to the country's broader socioeconomic development objectives over the next decade.
contextoradditionalinfo: The programme is designed to address the need for structural economic transformation in Viet Nam by leveraging innovation and entrepreneurship as key drivers for sustainable growth.
